diff.title: Unloading, Count and Inspection
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving in Zone A for all inbound receipts. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.

2. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

3. Complete the document check before unloading. At receiving, the document check happens before unloading.

4. Assign the task only to inbound operators. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.

5. Position the vehicle at the assigned inbound dock and apply brakes and wheel chocks. Verify the dock leveller is secured before entering the trailer.

6. Unload pallets to the Zone A inspection lane by load reference. Keep inbound pallets clear of outbound staging and main aisles.

7. Count every pallet, carton and unit against the delivery note and purchase order. Record shortages, overages and visible damage immediately in the WMS using a handheld WMS scanner.

8. Draw handheld WMS scanners from the shared pool. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Return each scanner to its charging dock after use and report faults to the shift supervisor.

9. Inspect all inbound goods before system booking. Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system.

10. Check each pallet for:
  a) correct product code, batch and quantity;
  b) intact packaging, seals and labelling;
  c) signs of damage, leakage, contamination or temperature abuse;
  d) pallet integrity and stability.

11. Verify pallet weight at inspection. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Reject or reconfigure overweight pallets and record the action on the goods receipt.

12. Segregate non-conforming goods in Zone A:
  a) move damaged or suspect stock to the quarantine area;
  b) attach a hold label with reason, quantity, date and operator initials;
  c) notify the shift supervisor for disposition.

13. Photograph damage where required and file images against the receipt number. Do not book damaged stock into available inventory.

14. Obtain inbound operator sign-off on the count and inspection record. Pass only inspected and accepted quantities forward for system booking and release to put-away.

15. Leave Zone A clear, sweep debris and remove banding and shrink wrap to designated waste containers. Report any spill, unsafe packaging or vehicle defect to the shift supervisor before releasing the dock.

diff.title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
diff.before:
1. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.

Zone B holds the site's primary pallet inventory. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets. All put-away to this zone follows PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away.

Do not move goods to Zone B until the WMS booking is confirmed. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Use the designated main transport aisles to transfer booked pallets from receiving into Zone B.

3. Observe bay load and pallet weight limits in every location.

Check the bay label before placing stock. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Calculate the total bay load before adding a pallet and leave the bay empty if the limit would be exceeded.

4. Use the correct truck for the task and aisle.

Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Operate counterbalance forklifts in the main aisles and approach bays squarely. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for transport and low-level placement. The fleet has 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays. Select the reach truck for any placement above lower levels and verify capacity against pallet weight before lifting.

5. Apply block-stacking limits where free stacking is authorised.

Where pallets are approved for free block-stacking outside racking, observe both limits together. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Stop stacking when either limit is reached and report any leaning or damaged stack to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Maintain access and inspection readiness.

Keep main aisles and rack storage aisles clear of staging, waste or trailing equipment. Position pallets fully within beams with no overhang into the aisle envelope. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Do not use any bay marked as damaged or under inspection and log defects for the maintenance technician without delay.

diff.title: Cold Zone E
diff.before:
1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Hold only chilled product in Zone E and keep doors closed except for put-away and picking moves.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check the automated monitoring display on entry and do not store product if the reading is below the minimum.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times. Treat any reading above the maximum as an incident under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and notify the shift supervisor immediately.

4. Manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift. Record the manual reading, time and initials on the Zone E temperature log and countersign any corrective action.

5. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Keep chilled goods staged in Zone A only for the time needed to complete inspection.

6. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every chilled inbound. Prioritise chilled pallets for inspection and move them to Zone E without delay after release.

7. Complete system booking before put-away to storage. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for the booking sequence: goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.

8. Do not put away unbooked pallets to Zone E. Confirm the storage location in the WMS, then transport the pallet directly to the assigned cold location.

9. Observe the pallet limit for all Zone E put-away. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg; reject or split any pallet exceeding this weight before put-away.

10. Store pallets to preserve airflow and temperature stability. Keep pallets off door thresholds, maintain circulation gaps and return monitoring probes to position after each move.

11. Report any temperature alarm, door fault or product exposure to the shift supervisor for review under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Quarantine affected stock and do not pick or dispatch until cleared.

diff.title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
diff.before:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep its three functions physically separate and clearly signed: the quarantine area, the returns inspection area and the hazmat cage.

2. The quarantine area is in Zone F. Use it only for goods held under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and for any stock awaiting a quality or stock-controller decision. Do not put away quarantined pallets to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E. Do not release quarantined stock until the hold is lifted in the system.

3. Inspect all returns in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item. Place the inspected goods in the quarantine area when they cannot be returned directly to stock. Obtain the required approval before any restock, rework or scrap decision.

4. Handle damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Move damaged pallets to the quarantine area in Zone F immediately. Record the damage, quantity and location in the WMS. Do not dispose, rework or restock until the authorised approver has signed the disposition.

5. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and is locked at all times except during authorised put-away or picking. Permit entry only to trained operators listed on the hazmat authorisation roster. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every movement, storage check and spill.

6. Observe the stock limit for the hazmat cage at all times:
   a) No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
   b) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1,000 kg.
   c) The hazmat cage therefore holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Calculate the remaining capacity before each put-away and do not exceed the 4,000 kg limit, even if floor space remains.

7. Complete system booking before any put-away to the cage. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Then execute PR-02 Put-away to storage:
   a) Verify the booking, hazard class and weight on the handheld.
   b) Transport the pallet to Zone F on the designated hazmat route.
   c) Place the pallet only in the assigned cage location and confirm the put-away by scan.

8. Maintain segregation and housekeeping in Zone F:
   a) Never store hazmat outside the cage, even temporarily.
   b) Never store non-hazmat goods inside the cage.
   c) Keep spill kits, fire extinguishers and safety data sheets at the cage entrance as defined in PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
   d) Keep the quarantine area clear of outbound staging. Outbound staging uses the area in front of docks 5-8. There are 4 outbound dock doors and outbound loads are not to be staged in Zone F.

9. Report any over-limit, damaged packaging or suspected leak in Zone F to the shift supervisor immediately and initiate PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Do not attempt to move leaking containers without the correct PPE and containment.

diff.title: Packing, Labelling and Wrapping in Zone D
diff.before:
1. Scope and control. This section governs PR-05 Packing and labelling and the transfer to PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Complete PR-05 in full before releasing any load under PR-06.

2. Location. Perform all packing, labelling and wrapping in Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Do not pack or stage outbound loads at other doors; dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.

3. Separation from value-added work. Keep standard dispatch packing in Zone D only. Zone F holds the value-added services area for rework, kitting and other non-standard activities. Move a unit to Zone F only when a value-added instruction applies.

4. Personal protective equipment. Wear required PPE at all times on the warehouse floor in Zone D:
   a) High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
   b) Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
   Do not enter packing lanes without both items.

5. Verification before packing. Apply the fixed sequence for PR-05. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing. Complete scan verification, resolve any short or mismatch, and only then start packing and labelling. Never pack unverified picks.

6. Packing and labelling instructions:
   a) Check the order and carton against the WMS task.
   b) Select the correct carton, pallet or tote for the order profile.
   c) Apply the customer label, carrier label and any handling label straight, fully adhered and scannable. Ensure barcodes face outward.
   d) Seal cartons and secure goods to prevent movement in transit.

7. Pallet building and weight limit. Build stable, stackable pallets in Zone D outbound staging.
   a) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Do not exceed this limit for any pallet released to dispatch.
   b) Distribute weight evenly, keep the footprint within the pallet, and use interlayer sheets where required.
   c) Rebuild any unstable or overweight pallet before wrapping.

8. Stretch wrapping. Wrap every outbound pallet prior to staging:
   a) Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D. Queue pallets to the next available wrapper; do not wrap by hand where a wrapper is specified.
   b) Apply the prescribed wrap pattern and containment force for the load type.
   c) Inspect the finished wrap for tears, exposed corners or loose tails. Rewrap defective loads.

9. Waste and housekeeping. Flatten all scrap cartons immediately and feed them to the site baler. The site has 1 cardboard baler. Keep Zone D aisles, wrappers and staging lanes clear of loose cardboard, banding and film.

10. Staging for PR-06. After wrapping, place labelled pallets in the allocated outbound staging lane in Zone D in dock-door sequence. Confirm door assignment for docks 5-8 and load number with PR-06 documentation before moving pallets to the dock. Do not block levellers or pedestrian routes while staging.

diff.title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
diff.before:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.
2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.
3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.
4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.
5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.
6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 24000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).
7. Load the delivery van within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 1200 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.
8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
9. Calculate outbound capacity on full-weight pallets. With 4 doors each handling 3 loads of 24 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift.
10. Respect hazmat constraints when staging mixed loads. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage inside Zone F at one time. At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). Do not allocate hazmat pallets to a trailer until cage stock is confirmed within limit.
11. Record trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts in the WMS before releasing the vehicle. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

diff.title: Electric Fleet
diff.before:
1. Fleet inventory for internal transport is fixed and fully electric for powered trucks. Do not exceed rated capacities or site weight limits when planning lifts and storage.

2. Counterbalance forklifts: the fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts. Each unit is rated at 2.5 t. Use these trucks for dock work, yard movements and bulk transport between zones.

3. Reach trucks: the fleet has 4 reach trucks for the high bays. Each reach truck is rated at 1.6 t. Reserve reach trucks for racking operations in the high-bay areas where height and aisle width require them.

4. Electric pallet jacks: the fleet has 8 electric pallet jacks. Assign these units to horizontal movements of full pallets, replenishment support and outbound staging.

5. Hand pallet jacks: the site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Keep these units distributed across receiving, picking and dispatch for short moves and manual handling where powered equipment is not required.

6. Personnel authorised to operate this equipment are defined by role. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. No other role may operate MHE unless authorised separately.

7. Pallet weight limit applies to every load moved by any truck. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Check the declared weight in the WMS before lifting and reject any pallet stated above this limit for standard handling.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.

diff.title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every activity in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.

2. Maintain the cold zone within its limits at all times. Keep the temperature at or above +2 °C. Keep the temperature at or below +8 °C.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Record the reading, the time and the verifier on the shift log. Do not rely on automated monitoring alone.

4. Respond immediately to any temperature alarm or out-of-range reading under PR-12 Cold-chain handling:
   a) Recheck the reading at the calibrated display inside Zone E.
   b) Keep doors closed and restrict entry while the check is repeated.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
   d) Hold affected stock inside Zone E and tag it pending decision.
   e) Do not move chilled goods to another zone until the shift supervisor authorises release.

5. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to all hazmat receipts, storage and movements. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

6. Observe storage limits for the hazmat cage. Store no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Calculate capacity on full-weight pallets: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg, so the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.

7. Stage hazmat only inside the cage. Do not exceed the floor limit. Keep incompatible classes segregated in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response safety data sheets.

8. Execute spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response as follows:
   a) Stop work and alert nearby personnel.
   b) Notify the shift supervisor immediately for incident response.
   c) Ventilate the area and isolate the spill. Do not wash spills into drains.
   d) Don appropriate PPE and deploy the spill kit for the material class.
   e) Contain, absorb and collect the material for safe disposal. Log the incident, quantity and corrective action.

9. Record every PR-12 Cold-chain handling verification and every PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response event in the WMS. Report any limit breach, equipment fault or stock at risk to the shift supervisor for follow-up.

2. Store hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Do not stage hazmat in receiving, bulk storage, picking or dispatch.

3. Do not exceed 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage total in the WMS before booking any inbound hazmat for put-away.

4. Obey the pallet limit. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. At this maximum weight the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Report any overweight pallet to the shift supervisor immediately and do not place it in the cage until approved.

5. Wear mandatory PPE on the warehouse floor at all times when handling or working near hazmat. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

6. Follow PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for all hazmat movements, segregation and spill response. Do not open, decant or rework hazmat outside the designated area in Zone F.

7. If a leak, spill or strong odour occurs, stop work and alert persons nearby. Notify the shift supervisor, ventilate and isolate the area, and keep all persons clear of the spill.

8. Do not attempt clean-up without correct PPE and equipment. Don PPE and deploy the spill kit only when authorised, then contain, absorb, collect and log the incident as directed under PR-13.

9. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The warehouse manager retains final sign-off for hazmat storage arrangements and safety controls in Zone F.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Report any damage to the hazmat cage, bunding, signage or ventilation to the maintenance technician and the shift supervisor without delay, and do not use defective equipment.

diff.title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply these limits to all racking in Zone B and to any free block stack on the floor. No pallet, including its load, may weigh more than 1,000 kg.

2. Do not exceed the rack bay limit. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Check the bay load plate before placing pallets and count the gross weight of every pallet in the bay against this limit.

3. Because the maximum pallet weight is 1,000 kg, a bay loaded with full-weight pallets can hold no more than two pallets. Three pallets at 1,000 kg would exceed 2,700 kg and is prohibited. Reduce the number of pallets or the weight per pallet to stay within the limit.

4. Observe equipment limits when handling stock for racking:
   a) Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t.
   b) Reach trucks for the high bays are rated at 1.6 t.
   Do not use equipment beyond its rated capacity to place or retrieve pallets.

5. Respect free block-stacking limits where pallets are not racked:
   a) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
   b) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
   Both limits apply at the same time. Stop stacking when either limit is reached. Stack only on a level, stable floor and interlock tiers where the product allows.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Use only designated pallet positions in Zone B and do not stage unracked pallets in rack aisles.

7. Keep aisles clear for safe transport and access:
   a) Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
   b) Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
   Do not encroach on aisle markings with overhanging pallets, wrappers or staging. Maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.

8. Report any rack damage immediately. Do not load, unload or pass under a damaged bay. Segregate the bay and apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for any affected stock. Move damaged or suspect pallets to the quarantine process and do not return them to racking until inspected.

9. Maintain racking integrity through scheduled checks. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Cooperate with the inspection and remove loads as directed to allow access.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Log every defect, impact and repair on the racking and equipment register and retain the record for review.

diff.title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
diff.before:
1. The dispatcher is accountable for outbound flow from Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Duties of the dispatcher are:
   1. Book transport for all outbound orders.
   2. Assign dock doors and time slots to carriers.
   3. Release outbound loads under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only when loads are complete and documented.

3. Operate the building's 8 dock doors as a single coordinated plan:
   1. Reserve dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving.
   2. Reserve dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch.
   3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for scheduling.

4. Own the dock schedule:
   1. Assign each carrier a specific door number and time slot.
   2. Balance demand across doors to maintain throughput.
   3. Communicate door assignments to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carriers before loading.

5. Enforce staging discipline in Zone D:
   1. Stage only verified and packed pallets in outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
   2. Do not release loads where picked items have not been scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-04 and PR-05.

6. Apply load limits on every booking:
   1. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg.
   2. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions.
   3. A trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets, being payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
   4. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions.
   5. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

7. Plan shift capacity to the proven maximum:
   1. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
   2. With 4 outbound dock doors, each taking at most 24 full-weight pallets per trailer, outbound capacity is at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift.
   3. Do not overbook beyond this limit. Split excess volume to the next shift or add trailer capacity with warehouse manager agreement.

8. Execute PR-06 Outbound dispatch as follows:
   1. Confirm order completeness and packing completion before assigning a door.
   2. Assign door and time slot and record them in the system.
   3. Release the load only after loading and door checks are complete.

9. Coordinate handover at shift change:
   1. Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors.
   2. Hand over open bookings, door allocations, delayed trailers and van commitments.
   3. Ensure no carrier arrives without a confirmed door and time slot.

diff.title: 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits
2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
diff.before:
1. Purpose of the role: unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage, and transfer accepted stock to the correct storage zone without breach of weight, temperature or hazmat limits.

2. Work location and scope: operate solely in Zone A, the receiving zone covering inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving; do not receive inbound goods at any other door. Hand over released pallets only to the designated storage zones: Zone B for bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.

3. Personal compliance on the warehouse floor: wear high-visibility vests at all times as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, and wear safety footwear class S3 as mandatory on the warehouse floor. Remain clear of moving MHE and follow pedestrian controls when working around docks 1-4.

4. Execute PR-01 Inbound receiving in the fixed sequence. Complete the document check BEFORE unloading. Verify purchase order, carrier, quantities and delivery notes against the load while the trailer remains closed. Report discrepancies before breaking the seal or starting unloading.

5. Unload, count and inspect goods in Zone A after the document check passes. Open, count and examine condition, quantity and labelling. Reject damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock from booking and segregate it for quarantine instruction. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01. Do not pre-book unchecked pallets.

6. Use WMS control correctly. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Log counts, inspection results and pallet IDs on the handheld scanner only after physical inspection is complete. Do not create system stock before inspection.

7. Observe pallet limits before release. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Check declared weight, re-weigh where required, and do not release overweight pallets for put-away. Report any overweight pallet to the supervisor for correction before PR-02 actions continue.

8. Perform PR-02 Put-away to storage only after system booking. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Print and apply system-directed labels, confirm location tasks on the scanner, and move pallets to the WMS-directed bay in Zone B or other assigned zone. Do not stage inbound stock in aisles or dispatch areas as put-away.

9. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for chilled inbound. Transfer accepted chilled goods immediately to Zone E, the cold zone held at +2 to +8 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C. Keep cold-chain pallets closed, minimise door openings, and record handover to Zone E so temperature control is maintained.

10. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for hazmat receipts. Route directed hazmat to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The hazmat cage covers 60 m2 inside Zone F and no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage stock on the WMS before put-away and do not exceed the limit. If leaking, odorous or damaged hazmat is found, stop work, contain the area and alert the shift supervisor; do not inspect or open damaged hazmat on the general bench.

11. Maintain inbound discipline: keep Zone A clear for inspection and unloading, return equipment and scanners to charge, and ensure all inspected goods are either booked and tasked for put-away or formally segregated before leaving the zone at shift end.

diff.title: 3.2 Returns and Packing Staff - Returns Inspection and Packing

diff.title: 1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs
diff.before:
1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs

Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates receiving from its 6,000 m2 warehouse floor. The building provides 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller, and inbound receiving is confined to a defined allocation and sequence.

1. Door allocation for inbound. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving exclusively. No inbound unloading will be scheduled to other doors.
2. Receiving hours. Standard receiving windows align with staffed shifts:
   a) Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
   b) Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
   Arrivals outside these windows or requiring extended handling will be accepted only where overtime has been agreed in advance. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3. Scheduling ownership. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and for inbound this includes confirming the allocated door in Zone A and the booked arrival slot before arrival.
4. Resource commitment. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Harborwick commits trained inbound operators to each booked receiving slot during the windows above.
5. Receiving sequence under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Harborwick will apply the following mandatory order for every inbound load:
   a) Document check happens before unloading.
   b) Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system.
   No goods will be unloaded prior to document verification, and no system receipt will be posted prior to physical inspection and count.
6. Booking to put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage. Put-away from Zone A to bulk or other storage will commence only after the WMS receipt is created under PR-01.
7. Load limits applicable at receiving. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Harborwick will weigh-check and reject or rework overweight pallets at Zone A before system booking, and will notify the client of any non-conformance identified during inspection.

Commitment: Harborwick will make Zone A and dock doors 1-4 available as scheduled, staff receiving with inbound operators during Shift 1 and Shift 2, and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage in the exact order stated above for every inbound delivery.

diff.title: 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release
diff.before:
Harborwick 3PL Ltd. commits to dispatch operations from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors.

1. Order preparation starts in Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, where pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2. Pick faces are replenished under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces before the picking shift starts. PR-04 Order picking is then executed on replenished faces.
3. Picked items are scan-verified before packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling. No order proceeds to PR-05 Packing and labelling without scan verification.
4. Packing, labelling and wrapping for PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-06 Outbound dispatch are completed in Zone D. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D for outbound pallets.
5. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers for docks 5-8 and confirms door assignment before loading.

Shift capacity is measured per operating shift. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

6. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. With 4 outbound doors, total outbound throughput is scheduled on this basis.
7. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions. A trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets, calculated as payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
8. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
9. Outbound capacity is at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors multiplied by loads per shift multiplied by pallets per trailer. Harborwick will not schedule beyond this limit without prior agreement.
10. Loads are released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only after packing and verification under PR-05 Packing and labelling are complete, pallets are wrapped, and door checks are satisfied. The dispatcher is the sole role to release the vehicle for departure.

diff.title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 24000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1200 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 1000 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 3 loads per shift multiplied by 24 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation.

diff.title: 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
diff.before:
2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level

1. Picking operations are performed in Zone C, which is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and no picking is performed from bulk storage locations.

2. Harbourwick commits to full scan-verified picking for every order under PR-04 Order picking. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and no tote or order will be released to packing without successful WMS verification. Packing and labelling under PR-05 Packing and labelling is then completed as a committed service step prior to dispatch.

3. Pick face availability is assured through PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, and picking will not commence on incomplete faces. This sequencing ensures order accuracy and prevents short picks due to empty locations.

4. The facility supporting this service level comprises a warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 with high-bay pallet racking in Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, providing 2,400 pallet positions for reserve stock. Replenishment moves stock from Zone B to Zone C to maintain pick face accuracy.

5. To sustain accurate and safe picking, Harbourwick maintains compliant infrastructure and handling limits at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, with segregated pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m wide maintained and kept clear. MHE and pedestrian segregation is enforced to protect picking accuracy and prevent location errors.

6. Pallet and racking limits are enforced as part of inventory integrity. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg, and any pallet exceeding this limit will be held for rework and not made available for picking.

7. Picking is executed with 20 handheld WMS scanners shared by pickers and inbound staff, ensuring every pick movement is system-directed and verified. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, and will investigate any scan discrepancy, location error or quantity variance identified during PR-03 or PR-04 execution.

8. Harbourwick commits to maintaining stock controller oversight of all replenishment and picking accuracy exceptions, with accurate WMS stock reflecting verified picks, replenishments and packing activity in Zone C.

diff.title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. shall handle all damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and shall move such stock to quarantine on the same day it is identified.

2. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 shall be held in the quarantine area in Zone F until inspection, approval and posting are complete. Zone F holds the value-added services area and is the sole quarantine location for damaged goods pending disposition.

3. The quarantine process shall be controlled as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response shall be notified immediately of any damage and shall direct placement into the quarantine area in Zone F and review the related reports.
  b) The warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs shall retain final authority for write-offs above threshold and for overall compliance of quarantine handling.
  c) No quarantined stock shall be moved to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging without recorded approval under PR-09.

4. Write-off approvals for damaged goods shall follow defined financial thresholds:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
  b) Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves such cases.
  c) Harborwick shall not process any write-off above 500 EUR without that approval recorded in the system.

5. Where damaged goods include hazmat, Harborwick shall stage and store such stock only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and shall contain no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1,000 kg, therefore the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Harborwick commits to enforce this limit and to reject or re-allocate any quantity that would exceed it, reporting the condition immediately.

6. Harborwick shall maintain traceability of all quarantined stock in Zone F, including photographic evidence where required, WMS posting of inspection outcomes, and retention of labels for audit. Disposition to restock, rework or scrap shall only occur after the applicable approver under paragraph 4 has authorised it.

diff.title: Docks and Yard Access
diff.before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

diff.title: Replenishment of Pick Faces
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces to prepare all pick faces before any picking activity commences.
2. Complete replenishment BEFORE the picking shift starts.
3. Do not release picking tasks until the replenishment cycle is confirmed complete in the WMS.

  a. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks to move full pallets from bulk storage to the picking zone.

  a. Travel via main transport aisles where available. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.

  c. Observe forklift speed limits at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.
  d. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings and maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.

  b. Re-queue any short replenishments due to missing stock and escalate to the shift supervisor.

diff.title: Order Picking in Zone C
diff.before:
1. Purpose and scope
This instruction defines PR-04 Order picking in Zone C. It applies to all picking of customer orders from ground-level pick faces and flow racks.

2. Zone and tasking
1. Perform all picking activity only in Zone C. Zone C is the picking zone comprising ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
2. Pick customer orders in Zone C against WMS scanner tasks. Do not pick from paper lists or verbal instructions.
3. Log onto the WMS with your personal ID and accept the next scanner-directed task. Complete tasks in WMS sequence unless the shift supervisor reprioritises.
4. Pickers own picking execution against scanner tasks. The shift supervisor runs the shift and resolves exceptions on the floor.

3. Pre-start conditions
1. Verify that PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces is complete. Pick faces are replenished before the picking shift starts; do not commence PR-04 Order picking while replenishment is still in progress.
2. Collect a serviceable handheld WMS scanner. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; return the unit to the charging station when the task batch is complete.
3. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment before entering the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

4. Picking execution
1. Travel to the location directed by the scanner. Confirm the location label by scanning.
2. Pick the exact product, batch and quantity displayed. Scan each unit barcode as prompted.
3. Place picked items directly into the assigned tote or order carton. Do not consolidate multiple orders into a single tote.
4. If stock is missing, damaged or short, use the scanner exception code and leave the location as found. Do not substitute alternative stock.
5. Report any empty or low pick face to the shift supervisor for replenishment via PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces.

5. Scan verification and transfer to packing
1. Complete scan verification before packing. Picked items are scan-verified before packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling.
2. At the end of the pick path, confirm the tote with the scanner close function. The WMS will release the tote for PR-05 Packing and labelling only after verification succeeds.
3. Place verified totes onto the designated outbound conveyor or transfer trolley for Zone C. Do not stage unverified totes.

6. Movement in Zone C
1. Observe forklift and pallet jack traffic rules while picking. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.
2. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings in Zone C.
3. Keep pick aisles clear of empty pallets and shrink wrap. Return handling equipment to its lane after use.

diff.title: Staging and Load Release
diff.before:
1. Stage only finished pallets in Zone D. Place outbound pallets only in the outbound staging area in front of docks 5-8.

Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Do not use Zone D for picking, replenishment or returns staging. Keep staging lanes clear of empty pallets and packing waste.

2. Confirm PR-06 requirements are met before staging. Complete PR-05 Packing and labelling in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

Check each pallet is stretch-wrapped and carries its correct outbound label. Do not move pallets to staging if wrapping is incomplete or labels are missing. Reject any pallet that has not passed verification and return it to Zone D packing for correction.

3. Obtain dispatcher release for every load. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.

Do not move staged pallets to the dock or load a vehicle without an explicit release from the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers; follow the assigned slot and door exactly.

4. Confirm door assignment before moving to the dock. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. 

Request confirmation of the specific door among docks 5-8 for the released load. Move pallets to the dock only after door confirmation. Stage in the lane that feeds the confirmed door and keep other door approaches clear.

5. Prepare the dock leveller at the assigned door. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

Inspect the leveller and dock approach before travel. Ensure the leveller is seated, locked to the trailer bed and rated for the load. Report any defect to the shift supervisor and do not use a faulty leveller.

6. Obey speed limits when handling staged loads. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.

Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to pedestrians at all marked crossings. Approach staging lanes and outbound lanes at low speed and sound the horn where sight lines are restricted.

7. Observe the dock ramp limit. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

Align straight to the leveller, carry the load low and travel at creep speed onto the ramp. Do not brake sharply or turn on the leveller plate. Stop and re-align if the pallet overhangs the forks.

8. Release the load only on dispatcher instruction. Load in the sequence stated on the release and secure each row before moving the next.

Notify the dispatcher once the trailer is loaded and doors are closed. Leave the staging area clear for the next confirmed load.

diff.title: Speed Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply the limits in this section at all times when operating forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Pedestrians and operators share the same aisles and must work to PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

2. Do not exceed 10 km/h inside the building. This ceiling applies to every indoor area, including Zones A, B, C, D, E and F, and to all main and storage aisles.

3. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Reduce speed further when the yard is congested, when visibility is restricted, or when the surface is wet or uneven.

4. Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and at every pedestrian crossing. Give way to pedestrians on the segregated walkways and at aisle intersections.

5. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches at doors 1-8. Approach the leveller squarely, keep the forks low, and stop if the leveller plate is not fully seated.

6. Observe signage and floor markings at all zone transitions. If a lower limit is posted, follow the posted limit. Never use the outdoor limit indoors, and never use the indoor limit in pedestrian zones or on dock ramps.

7. Report any speeding, near miss or collision immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. Stop the truck safely, secure the load, and preserve the scene for inspection.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Provide the time, location, truck identification, load status and witness details to support the review under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

9. Enforce these limits through daily supervision, scanner and WMS route discipline, and the documented pre-use check required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Treat repeated non-compliance as a safety breach under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and remove the operator from MHE duties pending re-briefing.

10. Keep this section displayed with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at the MHE charging area and at each dock office so that indoor, outdoor, pedestrian zone and dock ramp limits remain visible on every shift.

diff.title: Pedestrian Safety Rules
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every entry to the warehouse floor.
2. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor. Do not enter or remain on the floor without it fastened and visible.
3. Wear safety footwear class S3 at all times on the warehouse floor. Replace damaged or non-compliant footwear before starting work.
4. Stay inside the marked pedestrian system. Keep to the segregated pedestrian walkways. These walkways are 1.2 m wide and are bounded by barriers and floor markings.
5. Stop at every pedestrian crossing and barrier gate. Make eye contact with the forklift operator and wait for the truck to halt before stepping out.
6. Never walk under raised forks or a raised load. Never climb on racking or dock levellers to pass a vehicle.
7. Observe forklift speed discipline at all times:
 a) Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.
 b) Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Expect trucks to be moving at this reduced speed and keep clear.
 c) Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Do not overtake or crowd trucks on ramps.
8. Keep pedestrian walkways clear. Do not stage pallets, cages, stretch wrap or waste in the 1.2 m walkways or across crossing sight lines. Return barriers and gates to the closed position after use.
9. Use designated pedestrian doors where provided. Do not use dock doors or vehicle aisles as shortcuts. Where a pedestrian must cross a vehicle aisle, use only the marked crossing.
10. Obey all audible and visual warnings. Stop when you hear a forklift horn or reverse alarm. Yield to forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks at all times.
11. Report every near miss, collision, trip or barrier damage immediately. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and reviews every incident report. Provide the location, time and vehicles or persons involved.
12. Cooperate with temporary controls during spills, rack repairs or evacuation drills. Follow the shift supervisor's instructions and any additional barriers, signs or spotters put in place under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

diff.before:

3. Fasten the seat belt before the truck moves. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning and inching to a rack face.

4. Observe rated capacities when planning lifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t; do not exceed the rated capacity for the truck in use.

5. Control speed to the posted limit for the area. Inside the building, forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h.

6. In the outdoor yard, reduce speed appropriately but forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h.

10. Enter rack storage aisles only when clear. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; keep forks low while travelling, sound the horn at blind intersections and stop for oncoming trucks.

11. Keep aisles free of obstructions. Do not stage pallets, waste or charging equipment in main aisles or storage aisles, and maintain clear sightlines at aisle ends and pedestrian crossings.

12. Report defects immediately and withdraw the truck from service until cleared. Record any rack strike, wheel damage or leveller fault and notify the shift supervisor, as racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and strikes must be logged for that inspection.

diff.title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
diff.before:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

diff.title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 24000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1200 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 26 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 312 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 3 loads per shift multiplied by 26 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 312 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

diff.title: Floor Zones A–F
diff.before:
1. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Inbound Operators work in Zone A to unload, count and inspect deliveries before booking. Vehicles assigned to Zone A use docks 1-4 only. No outbound staging takes place in Zone A.

2. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Put-away from Zone A moves directly to Zone B rack locations. Stock in Zone B supplies replenishment to Zone C. Access in Zone B follows rack aisle controls.

3. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers operate in Zone C against scanner tasks to fulfil customer orders. Replenishment keeps Zone C pick faces filled from Zone B. Packing preparation also starts from picks completed in Zone C.

4. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Outbound loads are staged, wrapped and released in Zone D. Dispatchers assign docks 5-8 for loading in Zone D. Carriers collect only from Zone D doors.

5. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Product requiring temperature control is stored only in Zone E. Doors to Zone E remain closed except for put-away and picking moves. Monitoring keeps Zone E within its +2 to +8 °C range.

6. Zone F holds the value-added services area. The quarantine area is in Zone F for holds pending release. Returns are inspected in Zone F before any disposition. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F for segregated storage. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

Circulation between zones uses the marked aisle network.

7. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. These aisles link Zone A through Zone B and Zone C to Zone D, with branches to Zone E and Zone F. Counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks use main transport aisles for longer moves. Keep main transport aisles clear of staging at all times.

8. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are located inside Zone B between high-bay runs. Only materials handling equipment and authorised persons enter rack storage aisles when handling pallets.

9. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Walkways provide protected routes through and around Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E and Zone F. Do not block segregated pedestrian walkways with pallets, cages or waste. Cross only at marked crossing points.

diff.title: System Booking and Release to Put-Away
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving to close the receiving task in Zone A and apply PR-02 Put-away to storage to release pallets to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. No pallet leaves Zone A for put-away until both procedures are satisfied in order.

2. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Complete the count and inspection fully and resolve discrepancies on the inbound paperwork before creating any system booking. Do not book damaged, short or unidentified stock as available.

3. Observe the booking sequence:
   a. Inspection, then system booking. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01.
   b. System booking, then put-away. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02.
   Follow this order for every pallet without exception.

4. Book receipts on the WMS using the handheld scanners. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; return the device to its charge bay after booking and report any scanning failure to the shift supervisor immediately. Enter the exact quantity verified at inspection, the pallet ID, and the storage requirement indicated on the purchase order or product master.

5. Assign the put-away destination at booking:
   a. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Use for general ambient pallets.
   b. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Use only for temperature-controlled product and confirm the cold-chain status is intact.
   c. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Use for labelling, kitting or other value-added work instructed on the receipt.
   Direct the forklift operator to the assigned zone on the WMS put-away task. Do not stage pallets for Zone B, Zone E or Zone F outside their designated lanes.

6. Route exceptions to quarantine or hazmat holding:
   a. Move any pallet failing inspection, requiring quality review, or awaiting approval to the quarantine area in Zone F. Hold it on system status quarantine.
   b. Move packaged hazardous material requiring segregation to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. Hold it on system status hazmat hold.
   Do not book quarantine or hazmat pallets as available for sale and do not put them away to Zone B or Zone E.

7. Release the put-away task only when the WMS shows status booked and the destination zone is confirmed. Attach the signed inbound receipt to the booking record in PR-01, then generate the PR-02 put-away task. Hand over the pallets with scanner confirmation at the Zone A boundary.

diff.title: Cold Zone E
diff.before:
1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Hold only chilled product in Zone E and keep doors closed except for put-away and picking moves.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check the automated monitoring display on entry and do not store product if the reading is below the minimum.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times. Treat any reading above the maximum as an incident under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and notify the shift supervisor immediately.

4. Manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift. Record the manual reading, time and initials on the Zone E temperature log and countersign any corrective action.

5. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Keep chilled goods staged in Zone A only for the time needed to complete inspection.

6. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every chilled inbound. Prioritise chilled pallets for inspection and move them to Zone E without delay after release.

7. Complete system booking before put-away to storage. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for the booking sequence: goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.

8. Do not put away unbooked pallets to Zone E. Confirm the storage location in the WMS, then transport the pallet directly to the assigned cold location.

9. Observe the pallet limit for all Zone E put-away. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg; reject or split any pallet exceeding this weight before put-away.

10. Store pallets to preserve airflow and temperature stability. Keep pallets off door thresholds, maintain circulation gaps and return monitoring probes to position after each move.

11. Report any temperature alarm, door fault or product exposure to the shift supervisor for review under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Quarantine affected stock and do not pick or dispatch until cleared.

diff.title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every activity in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.

2. Maintain the cold zone within its limits at all times. Keep the temperature at or above +2 °C. Keep the temperature at or below +8 °C.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Record the reading, the time and the verifier on the shift log. Do not rely on automated monitoring alone.

4. Respond immediately to any temperature alarm or out-of-range reading under PR-12 Cold-chain handling:
   a) Recheck the reading at the calibrated display inside Zone E.
   b) Keep doors closed and restrict entry while the check is repeated.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
   d) Hold affected stock inside Zone E and tag it pending decision.
   e) Do not move chilled goods to another zone until the shift supervisor authorises release.

5. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to all hazmat receipts, storage and movements. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

6. Observe storage limits for the hazmat cage. Store no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Calculate capacity on full-weight pallets: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, so the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.

7. Stage hazmat only inside the cage. Do not exceed the floor limit. Keep incompatible classes segregated in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response safety data sheets.

8. Execute spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response as follows:
   a) Stop work and alert nearby personnel.
   b) Notify the shift supervisor immediately for incident response.
   c) Ventilate the area and isolate the spill. Do not wash spills into drains.
   d) Don appropriate PPE and deploy the spill kit for the material class.
   e) Contain, absorb and collect the material for safe disposal. Log the incident, quantity and corrective action.

9. Record every PR-12 Cold-chain handling verification and every PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response event in the WMS. Report any limit breach, equipment fault or stock at risk to the shift supervisor for follow-up.

diff.title: 3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)
diff.before:
3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)

1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. This segregated chilled area operates inside the warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 and is reserved solely for goods requiring continuous chilled storage. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every entry, movement and storage activity affecting Zone E.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check that doors close fully after each transit and never wedge or prop them open. Report any ice build-up, seal damage or prolonged door opening that could drive temperature below the lower limit.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times. Treat any reading above this upper limit as a cold-chain deviation. Initiate the response required under PR-12 Cold-chain handling immediately and prevent further warm air ingress until the area has stabilised.

4. Verify temperature manually each shift. Observe the calibrated display inside Zone E, record the reading with time and initials in the shift log, and compare it against the +2 to +8 °C range. Escalate out-of-range results without delay and retain the record for traceability.

5. Minimise exposure and keep the chamber closed. Plan picks and put-away to reduce entries, enter only when the task is ready, and exit promptly after completion. Allow doors to self-close and confirm engagement before leaving the area.

6. Wear mandatory personal protection on every warehouse floor task, including all Zone E work. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and must be fully fastened and visible before entry.

7. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor, including inside the cold zone. Inspect footwear for secure fastening and intact soles, and move carefully where condensation or moisture may make surfaces slippery.

8. Limit Zone E access to personnel trained in PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Inform the supervisor before entering for extended tasks and maintain visual or radio contact so assistance can be summoned. Do not use the cold zone for breaks, storage of ambient goods or non-chilled equipment.

9. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Direct every temperature alarm, failed verification, access problem or incident inside Zone E to the shift supervisor for immediate review and coordinated response.

10. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Refer repeated deviations, equipment faults, unresolved alarms and any cold-chain risk affecting product integrity to the warehouse manager for decision and sign-off.

11. Contain suspected breaches inside Zone E. Hold affected stock in place, tag it clearly as pending cold-chain decision, and prevent movement to other zones until authorised release is given under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

diff.title: 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership
diff.before:
1. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2. Shift coverage is 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday for Shift 1 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday for Shift 2; the supervisor on duty is accountable for all floor activity during those hours.
3. Duties of the role:
  1) Direct forklift operators, pickers, inbound operators and other floor staff across all operating areas: Zone A the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, Zone B the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, Zone C the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks, Zone D the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, Zone E the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.
  2) Maintain discipline on PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and ensure briefings are completed at every handover.
  3) Enforce site PPE and MHE rules: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, and forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
  4) Verify operational checks on shift: cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift; confirm readings are logged and escalate deviations immediately.
4. Incident and emergency ownership:
  1) Review every incident report without exception and close actions with documented follow-up.
  2) Lead evacuations under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, account for staff at the assembly point and apply the sequence that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
  3) Ensure an evacuation drill runs every quarter and attendance and learnings are recorded.
5. Quality and compliance decisions:
  1) Approve the final disposition of inspected returns; returns are inspected in Zone F and the supervisor determines restock, rework or scrap.
  2) Hold all goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling in the quarantine area in Zone F.
  3) Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR; damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.
6. Site integrity:
  1) Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and defects are quarantined and reported.
  2) Coordinate with the dispatcher and warehouse manager to keep receiving, storage, picking and dispatch flows aligned across Zone A, Zone B, Zone C and Zone D.
