diff.title: 2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
diff.before:
1. Purpose of the role: unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage, and transfer accepted stock to the correct storage zone without breach of weight, temperature or hazmat limits.

2. Work location and scope: operate solely in Zone A, the receiving zone covering inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving; do not receive inbound goods at any other door. Hand over released pallets only to the designated storage zones: Zone B for bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.

3. Personal compliance on the warehouse floor: wear high-visibility vests at all times as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, and wear safety footwear class S3 as mandatory on the warehouse floor. Remain clear of moving MHE and follow pedestrian controls when working around docks 1-4.

4. Execute PR-01 Inbound receiving in the fixed sequence. Complete the document check BEFORE unloading. Verify purchase order, carrier, quantities and delivery notes against the load while the trailer remains closed. Report discrepancies before breaking the seal or starting unloading.

5. Unload, count and inspect goods in Zone A after the document check passes. Open, count and examine condition, quantity and labelling. Reject damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock from booking and segregate it for quarantine instruction. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01. Do not pre-book unchecked pallets.

6. Use WMS control correctly. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Log counts, inspection results and pallet IDs on the handheld scanner only after physical inspection is complete. Do not create system stock before inspection.

7. Observe pallet limits before release. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check declared weight, re-weigh where required, and do not release overweight pallets for put-away. Report any overweight pallet to the supervisor for correction before PR-02 actions continue.

8. Perform PR-02 Put-away to storage only after system booking. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Print and apply system-directed labels, confirm location tasks on the scanner, and move pallets to the WMS-directed bay in Zone B or other assigned zone. Do not stage inbound stock in aisles or dispatch areas as put-away.

9. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for chilled inbound. Transfer accepted chilled goods immediately to Zone E, the cold zone held at +2 to +8 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C. Keep cold-chain pallets closed, minimise door openings, and record handover to Zone E so temperature control is maintained.

10. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for hazmat receipts. Route directed hazmat to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The hazmat cage covers 60 m2 inside Zone F and no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage stock on the WMS before put-away and do not exceed the limit. If leaking, odorous or damaged hazmat is found, stop work, contain the area and alert the shift supervisor; do not inspect or open damaged hazmat on the general bench.

11. Maintain inbound discipline: keep Zone A clear for inspection and unloading, return equipment and scanners to charge, and ensure all inspected goods are either booked and tasked for put-away or formally segregated before leaving the zone at shift end.

diff.title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
diff.before:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

diff.title: Approvals and Accountability
diff.before:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. No other role carries this overall accountability.

2. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The shift supervisor exercises approval authority only within that shift and escalates all matters beyond the defined thresholds to the warehouse manager.

3. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. No stocktake is closed, posted or communicated to the client until that sign-off is obtained. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy through cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, but they do not hold sign-off authority.

4. Under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse manager approval. The threshold is applied as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
  b) The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR.
Submit the damage report, value calculation and photographs to the relevant approver before scrapping, disposal or system write-off. Do not split a single damage event to remain below the threshold.

5. Under PR-07 Returns handling, the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, but the disposition takes effect only after shift supervisor approval. Do not move inspected returns back to stock until approval is recorded.

6. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Request overtime in advance with reason, hours and staff required. Do not work or record overtime hours without written approval from the warehouse manager.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Submit all injuries, near misses, equipment damage and procedural deviations to the shift supervisor on duty. Carry out corrective actions assigned from that review and close the report only when the shift supervisor confirms completion.

8. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. No operator may drive counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks or other MHE until the warehouse manager has issued authorisation. Maintain the authorisation register centrally and withdraw authorisation where training or medical requirements lapse.

9. Accountability for communication at shift change rests with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Complete the handover record, note open approvals, pending write-offs and outstanding incident reviews, and obtain acknowledgement from the incoming shift supervisor.

diff.title: Shift Leadership and Dock Control
diff.before:
1. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The role provides continuous floor leadership across both operating windows.

2. Shift coverage is as follows:
 a. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
 b. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
 Each shift has a designated shift supervisor accountable for personnel deployment, task allocation and first response to operational and safety incidents during that shift.

3. The shift supervisor holds the following decision authorities on the floor:
 a. Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
 b. Approve the final disposition of inspected returns following inspection in Zone F.
 c. Review every incident report raised on shift.
 Escalations above these thresholds pass to the warehouse manager under Chapter 2.2.

4. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The function controls all vehicle movements to and from the building.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Allocation follows the fixed door designation:
 a. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving.
 b. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.
 No carrier may occupy a door without a scheduled assignment from the dispatcher.

6. Coordination between the shift supervisor and the dispatcher is mandatory at shift start, mid-shift and before end-of-shift handover:
 a. The dispatcher confirms the inbound and outbound door plan for doors 1-4 and 5-8.
 b. The shift supervisor confirms staffing for unloading in Zone A, replenishment and picking in Zones B and C, and staging in Zone D.
 c. Both roles align on priorities for delayed carriers, labour constraints and incident impacts.

7. During live operations, the shift supervisor retains authority for floor safety and manning, while the dispatcher retains authority for the door schedule. If a safety incident requires a door to be closed or a load to be held, the shift supervisor directs the immediate action and the dispatcher re-books the affected time slot.

8. All releases of outbound loads from Zone D remain with the dispatcher. Forklift operators and pickers must not release or dispatch a load without dispatcher authorisation, even when staging is complete.

diff.title: Disposition and Write-Offs
diff.before:
1. Apply this section to every decision made under PR-07 Returns handling and PR-09 Damaged-goods handling after inspection is complete.
2. Hold all goods awaiting a disposition decision in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not move goods to bulk storage, picking or dispatch while the decision is pending.
3. Keep the quarantine area segregated within Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, and maintain clear identification of each pallet or unit under review.
4. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the proposal in the WMS with the inspection notes and photographs.
5. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Do not action the proposal until inspection is closed and the proposal is logged.
6. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling. Obtain that approval before releasing goods from quarantine.
7. Execute the approved disposition exactly as instructed:
  a. Restock approved goods to the assigned storage location.
  b. Route rework goods to the designated work area in Zone F.
  c. Move scrap goods to the scrap holding point and book the write-off in the WMS.
8. Process damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling through quarantine in the same way. Segregate the damage, count and photograph it, and enter the estimated value.
9. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. Damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor.
10. Submit write-off requests as follows:
  a. For write-offs up to 500 EUR, the shift supervisor reviews the evidence and approves or rejects the write-off in the WMS.
  b. For write-offs above 500 EUR, the shift supervisor endorses the request and forwards it to the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, for final decision.
11. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and retains control of quarantine releases during that shift. Do not bypass the shift supervisor for returns disposition or for damaged-goods write-offs within the 500 EUR limit.
12. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Do not apply that authority to returns or damaged-goods decisions, which follow the thresholds in this section.

diff.title: Adjustments and Recounts
diff.before:
1. Apply this section to every variance found during PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Treat cycle-count variances and full stocktake variances under the same control.

2. Execute a recount before any adjustment. A second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted. Do not post the adjustment from the first count alone.

3. Assign accountability for accuracy to the stock controller. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Direct all count sheets, recount requests and system adjustments to the stock controller for verification.

4. Trigger recounts from daily cycle counts. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Raise a recount immediately when the first count does not match the system quantity, when the location holds damaged stock, or when the picker reports a short pick.

5. Isolate the location pending recount. Keep the pallet or bin on hold in the system. Do not move, pick, replenish or dispatch stock from that location until the recount is complete.

6. Perform the recount independently. Use the original count method and re-scan each item. Record the second quantity, the counter name and the time on the recount form and return it to the stock controller.

7. Verify and decide on adjustment. Instruct the stock controller to compare the first and second counts, investigate system movements, and determine the correct on-hand quantity. Post the stock adjustment in the WMS only after the recount result is verified.

8. Link stock adjustments that create damaged-goods write-offs to the approval threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

9. Route write-off approvals as follows. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval. Submit write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval. Do not scrap, donate or remove stock from the system without the applicable approval recorded.

10. Close stocktake results under final sign-off control. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Withhold system release and financial posting of annual stocktake adjustments until that sign-off is recorded for PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

diff.title: 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs
diff.before:
1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs

1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2. The scope of accountability covers the warehouse floor of 6,000 m2, the high-bay racking providing 2,400 pallet positions and the building with 8 dock doors.
3. Site operations run over two shifts, and the warehouse manager retains overall accountability for both:
   a. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
   b. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

4. The warehouse manager holds exclusive sign-off authorities that cannot be delegated:
   a. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
   b. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
   c. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
   d. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

5. The threshold for damaged-goods escalation is fixed. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and requests above that value are forwarded for final decision by the warehouse manager.

6. The warehouse manager owns compliance with sequencing controls for safety and inventory integrity:
   a. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, ensure a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted.
   b. Under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, ensure roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

7. The warehouse manager is responsible for periodic governance and documented assurance:
   a. Ensure a full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year and withhold release of the WMS for normal operations until sign-off is recorded.
   b. Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
   c. Ensure an evacuation drill runs every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

8. The warehouse manager maintains oversight of shift governance. PR-15 End-of-shift handover is applied at every change of supervisor, and the warehouse manager reviews handover records and incident outcomes to confirm that staffing, operational and safety issues are closed between Shift 1 and Shift 2.
9. The warehouse manager provides final accountability for site safety, including adherence to inventory adjustment discipline, evacuation discipline and authorisation controls for personnel and overtime.

diff.title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. shall handle all damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and shall move such stock to quarantine on the same day it is identified.

2. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 shall be held in the quarantine area in Zone F until inspection, approval and posting are complete. Zone F holds the value-added services area and is the sole quarantine location for damaged goods pending disposition.

3. The quarantine process shall be controlled as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response shall be notified immediately of any damage and shall direct placement into the quarantine area in Zone F and review the related reports.
  b) The warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs shall retain final authority for write-offs above threshold and for overall compliance of quarantine handling.
  c) No quarantined stock shall be moved to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging without recorded approval under PR-09.

4. Write-off approvals for damaged goods shall follow defined financial thresholds:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
  b) Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves such cases.
  c) Harborwick shall not process any write-off above 500 EUR without that approval recorded in the system.

5. Where damaged goods include hazmat, Harborwick shall stage and store such stock only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and shall contain no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, therefore the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Harborwick commits to enforce this limit and to reject or re-allocate any quantity that would exceed it, reporting the condition immediately.

6. Harborwick shall maintain traceability of all quarantined stock in Zone F, including photographic evidence where required, WMS posting of inspection outcomes, and retention of labels for audit. Disposition to restock, rework or scrap shall only occur after the applicable approver under paragraph 4 has authorised it.

diff.title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
diff.before:
1. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.

Zone B holds the site's primary pallet inventory. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets. All put-away to this zone follows PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away.

Do not move goods to Zone B until the WMS booking is confirmed. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Use the designated main transport aisles to transfer booked pallets from receiving into Zone B.

3. Observe bay load and pallet weight limits in every location.

Check the bay label before placing stock. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Calculate the total bay load before adding a pallet and leave the bay empty if the limit would be exceeded.

4. Use the correct truck for the task and aisle.

Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Operate counterbalance forklifts in the main aisles and approach bays squarely. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for transport and low-level placement. The fleet has 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays. Select the reach truck for any placement above lower levels and verify capacity against pallet weight before lifting.

5. Apply block-stacking limits where free stacking is authorised.

Where pallets are approved for free block-stacking outside racking, observe both limits together. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Stop stacking when either limit is reached and report any leaning or damaged stack to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Maintain access and inspection readiness.

Keep main aisles and rack storage aisles clear of staging, waste or trailing equipment. Position pallets fully within beams with no overhang into the aisle envelope. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Do not use any bay marked as damaged or under inspection and log defects for the maintenance technician without delay.

diff.title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
diff.before:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.
2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.
3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.
4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.
5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.
6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 24000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 26 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).
7. Load the delivery van within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 1200 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.
8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
9. Calculate outbound capacity on full-weight pallets. With 4 doors each handling 3 loads of 26 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 312 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 312 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.
10. Respect hazmat constraints when staging mixed loads. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage inside Zone F at one time. At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). Do not allocate hazmat pallets to a trailer until cage stock is confirmed within limit.
11. Record trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts in the WMS before releasing the vehicle. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.
diff.after:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

PR-05 Packing and labelling must be completed in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Every outbound pallet must be stretch-wrapped prior to placement in outbound staging. Do not stage unwrapped pallets.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Weigh-check any pallet suspected to be overweight. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Do not exceed either the payload limit or the floor positions. For full-weight pallets, plan to a maximum of 28 pallets per trailer.

7. Load the delivery van within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 1800 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.

Check both weight and floor positions before assigning the van. If the order exceeds 2 full-weight pallets, book trailer capacity and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.

8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.

Coordinate with the dispatcher to sequence bookings across the 4 outbound doors. Keep each door to its planned 3 loads per shift and avoid queuing trailers outside the assigned time slots.

9. Calculate outbound capacity on full-weight pallets. With 4 doors each handling 3 loads of 28 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 336 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 336 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

Do not exceed the calculated ceiling without prior agreement. Record all bookings in the WMS and refer excess demand to the next available shift.

10. Respect hazmat constraints when staging mixed loads. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage inside Zone F at one time. At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). Do not allocate hazmat pallets to a trailer until cage stock is confirmed within limit.

Stage hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Confirm the cage total is within limit before building any outbound hazmat load.

11. Record trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts in the WMS before releasing the vehicle. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

Trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts must be recorded in the WMS before the vehicle is released. Do not release until the dispatcher has verified the record and loading and door checks are complete.

diff.title: Electric Fleet
diff.before:
1. Fleet inventory for internal transport is fixed and fully electric for powered trucks. Do not exceed rated capacities or site weight limits when planning lifts and storage.

2. Counterbalance forklifts: the fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts. Each unit is rated at 2.5 t. Use these trucks for dock work, yard movements and bulk transport between zones.

3. Reach trucks: the fleet has 4 reach trucks for the high bays. Each reach truck is rated at 1.6 t. Reserve reach trucks for racking operations in the high-bay areas where height and aisle width require them.

4. Electric pallet jacks: the fleet has 8 electric pallet jacks. Assign these units to horizontal movements of full pallets, replenishment support and outbound staging.

5. Hand pallet jacks: the site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Keep these units distributed across receiving, picking and dispatch for short moves and manual handling where powered equipment is not required.

6. Personnel authorised to operate this equipment are defined by role. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. No other role may operate MHE unless authorised separately.

7. Pallet weight limit applies to every load moved by any truck. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check the declared weight in the WMS before lifting and reject any pallet stated above this limit for standard handling.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.

diff.title: Authorisation and Daily Checks
diff.before:
1. This section applies PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation to authorisation and daily checks for all powered MHE.
2. The fleet covered comprises 6 electric counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks for the high bays and 8 electric pallet jacks.
3. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
4. Do not operate any counterbalance forklift, reach truck or electric pallet jack without current authorisation under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
5. Present licence, training certificate and authorisation record for verification before first assignment.
6. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including all authorisations under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
7. Retain the signed authorisation on file and revoke operating rights immediately when training lapses or following unsafe operation.
8. Complete the documented pre-use check for every forklift each day.
9. Perform the daily forklift check BEFORE first use each day in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
10. Do not start the truck until the daily check is fully recorded and passed.
11. Inspect brakes, steering, tyres/wheels, forks, chains, mast, lights, horn, reversing alarm and emergency stop where fitted.
12. Test battery charge, connections and electrolyte indicators on electric trucks and confirm isolation switches function correctly.
13. Record defects on the daily check sheet and tag the truck out of service if any safety-critical fault is found.
14. Report the defect to the shift supervisor and notify the maintenance technician without delay.
15. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
16. Do not attempt field repairs; await release by the maintenance technician after the repair log entry.
17. File completed daily check sheets in the MHE control file for audit and retain in shift order.
18. Apply the same daily documented check discipline to reach trucks and electric pallet jacks before first use.

diff.title: Safe Operation
diff.before:
1. Follow PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for every truck movement inside the building, in the outdoor yard and on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

2. Restrict driving to authorised personnel only. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks; no other role may operate MHE.

3. Fasten the seat belt before the truck moves. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning and inching to a rack face.

4. Observe rated capacities when planning lifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t; do not exceed the rated capacity for the truck in use.

5. Control speed to the posted limit for the area. Inside the building, forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h.

6. In the outdoor yard, reduce speed appropriately but forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h.

7. At any marked pedestrian zone or crossing, slow further. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and give way to pedestrians.

8. Apply the same low-speed limit on dock infrastructure. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches; approach squarely and check that the leveller is fully seated before crossing.

9. Use the aisle network as marked. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide two-way travel for forklifts and pallet jacks.

10. Enter rack storage aisles only when clear. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; keep forks low while travelling, sound the horn at blind intersections and stop for oncoming trucks.

11. Keep aisles free of obstructions. Do not stage pallets, waste or charging equipment in main aisles or storage aisles, and maintain clear sightlines at aisle ends and pedestrian crossings.

12. Report defects immediately and withdraw the truck from service until cleared. Record any rack strike, wheel damage or leveller fault and notify the shift supervisor, as racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and strikes must be logged for that inspection.

diff.title: Racking and Equipment Maintenance
diff.before:

2. Assign the maintenance technician to maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and to log all repairs. Do not operate damaged racking, levellers or trucks until the maintenance technician has inspected and cleared them.
3. Carry out a documented safety inspection of all racking every month. Include uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, anchors and beam locks in Zone B and any other racked locations.

5. Log every repair against the original defect. State the fault found, parts fitted, date completed and name of the maintenance technician. Close the tag only when the repair is verified and the log is signed.

7. Apply block-stack limits where pallets are free block-stacked outside racking. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. Measure from floor to top of load. Restack any non-compliant stack before leaving the area.

diff.title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply these limits to all racking in Zone B and to any free block stack on the floor. No pallet, including its load, may weigh more than 900 kg.

2. Do not exceed the rack bay limit. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Check the bay load plate before placing pallets and count the gross weight of every pallet in the bay against this limit.

3. Because the maximum pallet weight is 900 kg, a bay loaded with full-weight pallets can hold no more than three pallets. Three pallets at 900 kg equals 2,700 kg and reaches the bay limit. Reduce the number of pallets or the weight per pallet to stay within the limit.

4. Observe equipment limits when handling stock for racking:
   a) Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t.
   b) Reach trucks for the high bays are rated at 1.6 t.
   Do not use equipment beyond its rated capacity to place or retrieve pallets.

5. Respect free block-stacking limits where pallets are not racked:
   a) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
   b) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
   Both limits apply at the same time. Stop stacking when either limit is reached. Stack only on a level, stable floor and interlock tiers where the product allows.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Use only designated pallet positions in Zone B and do not stage unracked pallets in rack aisles.

7. Keep aisles clear for safe transport and access:
   a) Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
   b) Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
   Do not encroach on aisle markings with overhanging pallets, wrappers or staging. Maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.

8. Report any rack damage immediately. Do not load, unload or pass under a damaged bay. Segregate the bay and apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for any affected stock. Move damaged or suspect pallets to the quarantine process and do not return them to racking until inspected.

9. Maintain racking integrity through scheduled checks. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Cooperate with the inspection and remove loads as directed to allow access.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Log every defect, impact and repair on the racking and equipment register and retain the record for review.

diff.title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
diff.before:
1. The dispatcher is accountable for outbound flow from Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Duties of the dispatcher are:
   1. Book transport for all outbound orders.
   2. Assign dock doors and time slots to carriers.
   3. Release outbound loads under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only when loads are complete and documented.

3. Operate the building's 8 dock doors as a single coordinated plan:
   1. Reserve dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving.
   2. Reserve dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch.
   3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for scheduling.

4. Own the dock schedule:
   1. Assign each carrier a specific door number and time slot.
   2. Balance demand across doors to maintain throughput.
   3. Communicate door assignments to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carriers before loading.

5. Enforce staging discipline in Zone D:
   1. Stage only verified and packed pallets in outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
   2. Do not release loads where picked items have not been scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-04 and PR-05.

6. Apply load limits on every booking:
   1. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
   2. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions.
   3. A trailer takes at most 26 full-weight pallets, being payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
   4. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions.
   5. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

7. Plan shift capacity to the proven maximum:
   1. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
   2. With 4 outbound dock doors, each taking at most 26 full-weight pallets per trailer, outbound capacity is at most 312 full-weight pallets per shift.
   3. Do not overbook beyond this limit. Split excess volume to the next shift or add trailer capacity beyond the 312 full-weight pallet per shift limit with warehouse manager agreement.

8. Execute PR-06 Outbound dispatch as follows:
   1. Confirm order completeness and packing completion before assigning a door.
   2. Assign door and time slot and record them in the system.
   3. Release the load only after loading and door checks are complete.

9. Coordinate handover at shift change:
   1. Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors.
   2. Hand over open bookings, door allocations, delayed trailers and van commitments.
   3. Ensure no carrier arrives without a confirmed door and time slot.

diff.title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 24000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1200 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 26 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 312 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 3 loads per shift multiplied by 26 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 312 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

diff.title: Docks and Yard Access
diff.before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

7. For outbound operations, stage loads in Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

PR-05 Packing and labelling must be completed in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Every outbound pallet must be stretch-wrapped prior to placement in outbound staging. Do not stage unwrapped pallets.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Weigh-check any pallet suspected to be overweight. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 4 loads per shift multiplied by 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

diff.title: Docks and Yard Access
diff.before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

10. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

diff.title: Speed Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply the limits in this section at all times when operating forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Pedestrians and operators share the same aisles and must work to PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

2. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. This ceiling applies to every indoor area, including Zones A, B, C, D, E and F, and to all main and storage aisles.

3. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Reduce speed further when the yard is congested, when visibility is restricted, or when the surface is wet or uneven.

4. Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and at every pedestrian crossing. Give way to pedestrians on the segregated walkways and at aisle intersections.

5. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches at doors 1-8. Approach the leveller squarely, keep the forks low, and stop if the leveller plate is not fully seated.

6. Observe signage and floor markings at all zone transitions. If a lower limit is posted, follow the posted limit. Never use the outdoor limit indoors, and never use the indoor limit in pedestrian zones or on dock ramps.

7. Report any speeding, near miss or collision immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. Stop the truck safely, secure the load, and preserve the scene for inspection.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Provide the time, location, truck identification, load status and witness details to support the review under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

9. Enforce these limits through daily supervision, scanner and WMS route discipline, and the documented pre-use check required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Treat repeated non-compliance as a safety breach under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and remove the operator from MHE duties pending re-briefing.

10. Keep this section displayed with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at the MHE charging area and at each dock office so that indoor, outdoor, pedestrian zone and dock ramp limits remain visible on every shift.

diff.title: Safe Operation
diff.before:
1. Follow PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for every truck movement inside the building, in the outdoor yard and on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

2. Restrict driving to authorised personnel only. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks; no other role may operate MHE.

3. Fasten the seat belt before the truck moves. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning and inching to a rack face.

4. Observe rated capacities when planning lifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t and reach trucks are rated at 2.0 t; do not exceed the rated capacity for the truck in use.

5. Control speed to the posted limit for the area. Inside the building, forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h.

6. In the outdoor yard, reduce speed appropriately but forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h.

7. At any marked pedestrian zone or crossing, slow further. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and give way to pedestrians.

8. Apply the same low-speed limit on dock infrastructure. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches; approach squarely and check that the leveller is fully seated before crossing.

9. Use the aisle network as marked. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide two-way travel for forklifts and pallet jacks.

10. Enter rack storage aisles only when clear. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; keep forks low while travelling, sound the horn at blind intersections and stop for oncoming trucks.

11. Keep aisles free of obstructions. Do not stage pallets, waste or charging equipment in main aisles or storage aisles, and maintain clear sightlines at aisle ends and pedestrian crossings.

12. Report defects immediately and withdraw the truck from service until cleared. Record any rack strike, wheel damage or leveller fault and notify the shift supervisor, as racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and strikes must be logged for that inspection.

3.3 Maintenance Technician - Equipment, Racking and Dock Maintenance
diff.before:
1. Maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and log all repairs across the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor.

2. Own the MHE fleet serviceability and availability. Service, inspect and repair 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Log every repair, parts replacement and safety adjustment in the maintenance register.

3. Support the daily control regime under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Ensure every forklift receives a documented pre-use check each day and that the daily forklift check happens before first use each day. Withdraw from service any truck that fails brakes, steering, hydraulics, lights, horn or seat belt function and tag it until cleared.

4. Maintain speed control and warning systems to enforce site limits. Calibrate and test limiters, signage and floor markings for: 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

5. Own racking integrity for all pallet positions. Conduct a documented safety inspection of racking every month and retain inspection records. Verify uprights, beams, bracing, floor fixings and load notices. Enforce that each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg and instruct immediate offload and reporting of any overload or impact damage.

6. Maintain aisle and walkway compliance under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Keep main transport aisles clear at 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles clear at 3.0 m wide and segregated pedestrian walkways clear at 1.2 m wide. Repaint markings, repair barriers and lighting and replace damaged signage without delay.

7. Maintain dock equipment for all 8 dock doors. Service and test each of the 8 dock levellers, seals, doors, controls and interlocks. Keep leveller pits clean, clear of debris and free of hydraulic leaks to preserve safe ramp operation.

Observe that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

diff.title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
diff.before:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

diff.title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 4 loads per shift multiplied by 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

diff.title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
diff.before:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep its three functions physically separate and clearly signed: the quarantine area, the returns inspection area and the hazmat cage.

2. The quarantine area is in Zone F. Use it only for goods held under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and for any stock awaiting a quality or stock-controller decision. Do not put away quarantined pallets to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E. Do not release quarantined stock until the hold is lifted in the system.

3. Inspect all returns in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item. Place the inspected goods in the quarantine area when they cannot be returned directly to stock. Obtain the required approval before any restock, rework or scrap decision.

4. Handle damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Move damaged pallets to the quarantine area in Zone F immediately. Record the damage, quantity and location in the WMS. Do not dispose, rework or restock until the authorised approver has signed the disposition.

5. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and is locked at all times except during authorised put-away or picking. Permit entry only to trained operators listed on the hazmat authorisation roster. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every movement, storage check and spill.

6. Observe the stock limit for the hazmat cage at all times:
   a) No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
   b) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
   c) The hazmat cage therefore holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Calculate the remaining capacity before each put-away and do not exceed the 4,000 kg limit, even if floor space remains.

7. Complete system booking before any put-away to the cage. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Then execute PR-02 Put-away to storage:
   a) Verify the booking, hazard class and weight on the handheld.
   b) Transport the pallet to Zone F on the designated hazmat route.
   c) Place the pallet only in the assigned cage location and confirm the put-away by scan.

8. Maintain segregation and housekeeping in Zone F:
   a) Never store hazmat outside the cage, even temporarily.
   b) Never store non-hazmat goods inside the cage.
   c) Keep spill kits, fire extinguishers and safety data sheets at the cage entrance as defined in PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
   d) Keep the quarantine area clear of outbound staging. Outbound staging uses the area in front of docks 5-8. There are 4 outbound dock doors and outbound loads are not to be staged in Zone F.

9. Report any over-limit, damaged packaging or suspected leak in Zone F to the shift supervisor immediately and initiate PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Do not attempt to move leaking containers without the correct PPE and containment.

diff.title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
diff.before:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

PR-05 Packing and labelling must be completed in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Every outbound pallet must be stretch-wrapped prior to placement in outbound staging. Do not stage unwrapped pallets.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Weigh-check any pallet suspected to be overweight. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

   a. Payload limit is 1800 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.

Check both weight and floor positions before assigning the van. If the order exceeds 2 full-weight pallets, book trailer capacity and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.

8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift.

Coordinate with the dispatcher to sequence bookings across the 4 outbound doors. Keep each door to its planned 4 loads per shift and avoid queuing trailers outside the assigned time slots.

At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). diff.title: Electric Fleet
diff.before:
1. Fleet inventory for internal transport is fixed and fully electric for powered trucks. Do not exceed rated capacities or site weight limits when planning lifts and storage.

2. Counterbalance forklifts: the fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts. Each unit is rated at 3.0 t. Use these trucks for dock work, yard movements and bulk transport between zones.

3. Reach trucks: the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays. Each reach truck is rated at 2.0 t. Reserve reach trucks for racking operations in the high-bay areas where height and aisle width require them.

4. Electric pallet jacks: the fleet has 11 electric pallet jacks. Assign these units to horizontal movements of full pallets, replenishment support and outbound staging.

5. Hand pallet jacks: the site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Keep these units distributed across receiving, picking and dispatch for short moves and manual handling where powered equipment is not required.

6. Personnel authorised to operate this equipment are defined by role. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. No other role may operate MHE unless authorised separately.

7. Pallet weight limit applies to every load moved by any truck. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check the declared weight in the WMS before lifting and reject any pallet stated above this limit for standard handling.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.
