diff.title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every activity in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.

2. Maintain the cold zone within its limits at all times. Keep the temperature at or above +2 °C. Keep the temperature at or below +6 °C.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Record the reading, the time and the verifier on the shift log. Do not rely on automated monitoring alone.

4. Respond immediately to any temperature alarm or out-of-range reading under PR-12 Cold-chain handling:
   a) Recheck the reading at the calibrated display inside Zone E.
   b) Keep doors closed and restrict entry while the check is repeated.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
   d) Hold affected stock inside Zone E and tag it pending decision.
   e) Do not move chilled goods to another zone until the shift supervisor authorises release.

5. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to all hazmat receipts, storage and movements. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

6. Observe storage limits for the hazmat cage. Store no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Calculate capacity on full-weight pallets: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, so the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.

7. Stage hazmat only inside the cage. Do not exceed the floor limit. Keep incompatible classes segregated in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response safety data sheets.

8. Execute spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response as follows:
   a) Stop work and alert nearby personnel.
   b) Notify the shift supervisor immediately for incident response.
   c) Ventilate the area and isolate the spill. Do not wash spills into drains.
   d) Don appropriate PPE and deploy the spill kit for the material class.
   e) Contain, absorb and collect the material for safe disposal. Log the incident, quantity and corrective action.

9. Record every PR-12 Cold-chain handling verification and every PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response event in the WMS. Report any limit breach, equipment fault or stock at risk to the shift supervisor for follow-up.

diff.before:

diff.title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
diff.before:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

diff.title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. shall handle all damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and shall move such stock to quarantine on the same day it is identified.

2. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 shall be held in the quarantine area in Zone F until inspection, approval and posting are complete. Zone F holds the value-added services area and is the sole quarantine location for damaged goods pending disposition.

3. The quarantine process shall be controlled as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response shall be notified immediately of any damage and shall direct placement into the quarantine area in Zone F and review the related reports.
  b) The warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs shall retain final authority for write-offs above threshold and for overall compliance of quarantine handling.
  c) No quarantined stock shall be moved to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging without recorded approval under PR-09.

4. Write-off approvals for damaged goods shall follow defined financial thresholds:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
  b) Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves such cases. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision.
  c) Harborwick shall not process any write-off above 750 EUR without that approval recorded in the system.

5. Where damaged goods include hazmat, Harborwick shall stage and store such stock only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and shall contain no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, therefore the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Harborwick commits to enforce this limit and to reject or re-allocate any quantity that would exceed it, reporting the condition immediately.

6. Harborwick shall maintain traceability of all quarantined stock in Zone F, including photographic evidence where required, WMS posting of inspection outcomes, and retention of labels for audit. Disposition to restock, rework or scrap shall only occur after the applicable approver under paragraph 4 has authorised it.

diff.title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
diff.before:
1. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.

Zone B holds the site's primary pallet inventory. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets. All put-away to this zone follows PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away.

Do not move goods to Zone B until the WMS booking is confirmed. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Use the designated main transport aisles to transfer booked pallets from receiving into Zone B.

3. Observe bay load and pallet weight limits in every location.

Check the bay label before placing stock. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Calculate the total bay load before adding a pallet and leave the bay empty if the limit would be exceeded.

4. Use the correct truck for the task and aisle.

Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Operate counterbalance forklifts in the main aisles and approach bays squarely. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for transport and low-level placement. The fleet has 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays. Select the reach truck for any placement above lower levels and verify capacity against pallet weight before lifting.

5. Apply block-stacking limits where free stacking is authorised.

Where pallets are approved for free block-stacking outside racking, observe both limits together. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Stop stacking when either limit is reached and report any leaning or damaged stack to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Maintain access and inspection readiness.

Keep main aisles and rack storage aisles clear of staging, waste or trailing equipment. Position pallets fully within beams with no overhang into the aisle envelope. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Do not use any bay marked as damaged or under inspection and log defects for the maintenance technician without delay.

diff.title: Racking and Equipment Maintenance
diff.before:
1. Maintain racking, MHE and dock equipment to a safe, serviceable standard. Keep all storage within rated limits and keep a complete record of inspections and repairs.
2. Assign the maintenance technician to maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and to log all repairs. Do not operate damaged racking, levellers or trucks until the maintenance technician has inspected and cleared them.
3. Carry out a documented safety inspection of all racking every month. Include uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, anchors and beam locks in Zone B and any other racked locations.
4. Record the monthly inspection by bay, level and date. Photograph defects, grade the damage and tag the bay out of use where required. Enter the result in the repair log on the same day.
5. Log every repair against the original defect. State the fault found, parts fitted, date completed and name of the maintenance technician. Close the tag only when the repair is verified and the log is signed.
6. Enforce bay load limits at all times. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Do not exceed the posted bay label. Redistribute or offload overweight bays immediately and report the occurrence for correction.
7. Apply block-stack limits where pallets are free block-stacked outside racking. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. Measure from floor to top of load. Restack any non-compliant stack before leaving the area.
8. Include MHE and dock equipment in the inspection cycle. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts and the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays; check steering, brakes, forks, chains, hydraulics and safety devices. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; check leveller plates, lips, pits, controls and edge guards.
9. Coordinate MHE checks with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Report defects found during daily checks under PR-10 to the maintenance technician without delay. Take unserviceable trucks out of service, isolate the keys and update the log.
10. Review the repair log at each monthly inspection. Verify that outstanding actions are closed, recurring damage is investigated and preventive measures are applied to protect racking and equipment.

diff.title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply these limits to all racking in Zone B and to any free block stack on the floor. No pallet, including its load, may weigh more than 900 kg.

2. Do not exceed the rack bay limit. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Check the bay load plate before placing pallets and count the gross weight of every pallet in the bay against this limit.

3. Because the maximum pallet weight is 900 kg, a bay loaded with full-weight pallets can hold no more than three pallets. Three pallets at 900 kg equals 2,700 kg and reaches the bay limit. Reduce the number of pallets or the weight per pallet to stay within the limit.

4. Observe equipment limits when handling stock for racking:
   a) Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t.
   b) Reach trucks for the high bays are rated at 2.0 t.
   Do not use equipment beyond its rated capacity to place or retrieve pallets.

5. Respect free block-stacking limits where pallets are not racked:
   a) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
   b) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
   Both limits apply at the same time. Stop stacking when either limit is reached. Stack only on a level, stable floor and interlock tiers where the product allows.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Use only designated pallet positions in Zone B and do not stage unracked pallets in rack aisles.

7. Keep aisles clear for safe transport and access:
   a) Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
   b) Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
   Do not encroach on aisle markings with overhanging pallets, wrappers or staging. Maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.

8. Report any rack damage immediately. Do not load, unload or pass under a damaged bay. Segregate the bay and apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for any affected stock. Move damaged or suspect pallets to the quarantine process and do not return them to racking until inspected.

9. Maintain racking integrity through scheduled checks. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Cooperate with the inspection and remove loads as directed to allow access.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Log every defect, impact and repair on the racking and equipment register and retain the record for review.

diff.title: 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits
2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
diff.before:
2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level

1. Picking operations are performed in Zone C, which is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and no picking is performed from bulk storage locations.

2. Harbourwick commits to full scan-verified picking for every order under PR-04 Order picking. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and no tote or order will be released to packing without successful WMS verification. Packing and labelling under PR-05 Packing and labelling is then completed as a committed service step prior to dispatch.

3. Pick face availability is assured through PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, and picking will not commence on incomplete faces. This sequencing ensures order accuracy and prevents short picks due to empty locations.

4. The facility supporting this service level comprises a warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 with high-bay pallet racking in Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, providing 2,400 pallet positions for reserve stock. Replenishment moves stock from Zone B to Zone C to maintain pick face accuracy.

5. To sustain accurate and safe picking, Harbourwick maintains compliant infrastructure and handling limits at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, with segregated pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m wide maintained and kept clear. MHE and pedestrian segregation is enforced to protect picking accuracy and prevent location errors.

6. Pallet and racking limits are enforced as part of inventory integrity. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, and any pallet exceeding this limit will be held for rework and not made available for picking.

7. Picking is executed with 20 handheld WMS scanners shared by pickers and inbound staff, ensuring every pick movement is system-directed and verified. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, and will investigate any scan discrepancy, location error or quantity variance identified during PR-03 or PR-04 execution.

8. Harbourwick commits to maintaining stock controller oversight of all replenishment and picking accuracy exceptions, with accurate WMS stock reflecting verified picks, replenishments and packing activity in Zone C.

diff.title: Docks and Yard Access
diff.before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

7. For outbound operations, stage loads in Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

diff.title: Unloading, Count and Inspection
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving in Zone A for all inbound receipts. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.

2. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

3. Complete the document check before unloading. At receiving, the document check happens before unloading.

4. Assign the task only to inbound operators. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.

5. Position the vehicle at the assigned inbound dock and apply brakes and wheel chocks. Verify the dock leveller is secured before entering the trailer.

6. Unload pallets to the Zone A inspection lane by load reference. Keep inbound pallets clear of outbound staging and main aisles.

7. Count every pallet, carton and unit against the delivery note and purchase order. Record shortages, overages and visible damage immediately in the WMS using a handheld WMS scanner.

8. Draw handheld WMS scanners from the shared pool. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Return each scanner to its charging dock after use and report faults to the shift supervisor.

9. Inspect all inbound goods before system booking. Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system.

10. Check each pallet for:
  a) correct product code, batch and quantity;
  b) intact packaging, seals and labelling;
  c) signs of damage, leakage, contamination or temperature abuse;
  d) pallet integrity and stability.

11. Verify pallet weight at inspection. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Reject or reconfigure overweight pallets and record the action on the goods receipt.

12. Segregate non-conforming goods identified during inspection:
  a) move damaged or suspect stock to the quarantine area in Zone F;
  b) attach a hold label with reason, quantity, date and operator initials;
  c) notify the shift supervisor for disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

13. Photograph damage where required and file images against the receipt number. Do not book damaged stock into available inventory.

14. Obtain inbound operator sign-off on the count and inspection record. Pass only inspected and accepted quantities forward for system booking and release to put-away.

15. Leave Zone A clear, sweep debris and remove banding and shrink wrap to designated waste containers. Report any spill, unsafe packaging or vehicle defect to the shift supervisor before releasing the dock.

diff.title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
diff.before:
1. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.

Zone B holds the site's primary pallet inventory. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets. All put-away to this zone follows PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away.

Do not move goods to Zone B until the WMS booking is confirmed. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Use the designated main transport aisles to transfer booked pallets from receiving into Zone B.

3. Observe bay load and pallet weight limits in every location.

Check the bay label before placing stock. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Calculate the total bay load before adding a pallet and leave the bay empty if the limit would be exceeded.

4. Use the correct truck for the task and aisle.

Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Operate counterbalance forklifts in the main aisles and approach bays squarely. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for transport and low-level placement. The fleet has 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays. Select the reach truck for any placement above lower levels and verify capacity against pallet weight before lifting.

5. Apply block-stacking limits where free stacking is authorised.

Where pallets are approved for free block-stacking outside racking, observe both limits together. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Stop stacking when either limit is reached and report any leaning or damaged stack to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Maintain access and inspection readiness.

Keep main aisles and rack storage aisles clear of staging, waste or trailing equipment. Position pallets fully within beams with no overhang into the aisle envelope. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Do not use any bay marked as damaged or under inspection and log defects for the maintenance technician without delay.

diff.title: Cold Zone E
diff.before:
1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C. Hold only chilled product in Zone E and keep doors closed except for put-away and picking moves.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check the automated monitoring display on entry and do not store product if the reading is below the minimum.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +6 °C at all times. Treat any reading above the maximum as an incident under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and notify the shift supervisor immediately.

4. Manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift. Record the manual reading, time and initials on the Zone E temperature log and countersign any corrective action.

5. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Keep chilled goods staged in Zone A only for the time needed to complete inspection.

6. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every chilled inbound. Prioritise chilled pallets for inspection and move them to Zone E without delay after release.

7. Complete system booking before put-away to storage. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for the booking sequence: goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.

8. Do not put away unbooked pallets to Zone E. Confirm the storage location in the WMS, then transport the pallet directly to the assigned cold location.

9. Observe the pallet limit for all Zone E put-away. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg; reject or split any pallet exceeding this weight before put-away.

10. Store pallets to preserve airflow and temperature stability. Keep pallets off door thresholds, maintain circulation gaps and return monitoring probes to position after each move.

11. Report any temperature alarm, door fault or product exposure to the shift supervisor for review under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Quarantine affected stock and do not pick or dispatch until cleared.

diff.title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
diff.before:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep its three functions physically separate and clearly signed: the quarantine area, the returns inspection area and the hazmat cage.

2. The quarantine area is in Zone F. Use it only for goods held under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and for any stock awaiting a quality or stock-controller decision. Do not put away quarantined pallets to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E. Do not release quarantined stock until the hold is lifted in the system.

3. Inspect all returns in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item. Place the inspected goods in the quarantine area when they cannot be returned directly to stock. Obtain the required approval before any restock, rework or scrap decision.

4. Handle damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Move damaged pallets to the quarantine area in Zone F immediately. Record the damage, quantity and location in the WMS. Do not dispose, rework or restock until the authorised approver has signed the disposition.

5. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and is locked at all times except during authorised put-away or picking. diff.title: Packing, Labelling and Wrapping in Zone D
diff.before:
1. Scope and control. This section governs PR-05 Packing and labelling and the transfer to PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Complete PR-05 in full before releasing any load under PR-06.

2. Location. Perform all packing, labelling and wrapping in Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Do not pack or stage outbound loads at other doors; dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.

3. Separation from value-added work. Keep standard dispatch packing in Zone D only. Zone F holds the value-added services area for rework, kitting and other non-standard activities. Move a unit to Zone F only when a value-added instruction applies.

4. Personal protective equipment. Wear required PPE at all times on the warehouse floor in Zone D:
   a) High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
   b) Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
   Do not enter packing lanes without both items.

5. Verification before packing. Apply the fixed sequence for PR-05. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing. Complete scan verification, resolve any short or mismatch, and only then start packing and labelling. Never pack unverified picks.

6. Packing and labelling instructions:
   a) Check the order and carton against the WMS task.
   b) Select the correct carton, pallet or tote for the order profile.
   c) Apply the customer label, carrier label and any handling label straight, fully adhered and scannable. Ensure barcodes face outward.
   d) Seal cartons and secure goods to prevent movement in transit.

7. Pallet building and weight limit. Build stable, stackable pallets in Zone D outbound staging.
   a) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Do not exceed this limit for any pallet released to dispatch.
   b) Distribute weight evenly, keep the footprint within the pallet, and use interlayer sheets where required.
   c) Rebuild any unstable or overweight pallet before wrapping.

8. Stretch wrapping. Wrap every outbound pallet prior to staging:
   a) Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D. Queue pallets to the next available wrapper; do not wrap by hand where a wrapper is specified.
   b) Apply the prescribed wrap pattern and containment force for the load type.
   c) Inspect the finished wrap for tears, exposed corners or loose tails. Rewrap defective loads.

9. Waste and housekeeping. Flatten all scrap cartons immediately and feed them to the site baler. The site has 1 cardboard baler. Keep Zone D aisles, wrappers and staging lanes clear of loose cardboard, banding and film.

10. Staging for PR-06. After wrapping, place labelled pallets in the allocated outbound staging lane in Zone D in dock-door sequence. Confirm door assignment for docks 5-8 and load number with PR-06 documentation before moving pallets to the dock. Do not block levellers or pedestrian routes while staging.

diff.title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
diff.before:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

PR-05 Packing and labelling must be completed in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Every outbound pallet must be stretch-wrapped prior to placement in outbound staging. Do not stage unwrapped pallets.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Weigh-check any pallet suspected to be overweight. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Do not exceed either the payload limit or the floor positions. For full-weight pallets, plan to a maximum of 28 pallets per trailer.

7. Load the delivery van within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 1800 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.

Check both weight and floor positions before assigning the van. If the order exceeds 2 full-weight pallets, book trailer capacity and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.

8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift.

Coordinate with the dispatcher to sequence bookings across the 4 outbound doors. Keep each door to its planned 4 loads per shift and avoid queuing trailers outside the assigned time slots.

9. Calculate outbound capacity on full-weight pallets. With 4 doors each handling 4 loads of 28 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

Do not exceed the calculated ceiling without prior agreement. Record all bookings in the WMS and refer excess demand to the next available shift.

Stage hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Confirm the cage total is within limit before building any outbound hazmat load.

diff.title: Electric Fleet
diff.before:
1. Fleet inventory for internal transport is fixed and fully electric for powered trucks. Do not exceed rated capacities or site weight limits when planning lifts and storage.

2. Counterbalance forklifts: the fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts. Each unit is rated at 3.0 t. Use these trucks for dock work, yard movements and bulk transport between zones.

3. Reach trucks: the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays. Each reach truck is rated at 2.0 t. Reserve reach trucks for racking operations in the high-bay areas where height and aisle width require them.

4. Electric pallet jacks: the fleet has 11 electric pallet jacks. Assign these units to horizontal movements of full pallets, replenishment support and outbound staging.

5. Hand pallet jacks: the site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Keep these units distributed across receiving, picking and dispatch for short moves and manual handling where powered equipment is not required.

6. Personnel authorised to operate this equipment are defined by role. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. No other role may operate MHE unless authorised separately.

7. Pallet weight limit applies to every load moved by any truck. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check the declared weight in the WMS before lifting and reject any pallet stated above this limit for standard handling.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.

diff.title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every activity in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.

2. Maintain the cold zone within its limits at all times. Keep the temperature at or above +2 °C. Keep the temperature at or below +6 °C.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Record the reading, the time and the verifier on the shift log. Do not rely on automated monitoring alone.

4. Respond immediately to any temperature alarm or out-of-range reading under PR-12 Cold-chain handling:
   a) Recheck the reading at the calibrated display inside Zone E.
   b) Keep doors closed and restrict entry while the check is repeated.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
   d) Hold affected stock inside Zone E and tag it pending decision.
   e) Do not move chilled goods to another zone until the shift supervisor authorises release.

5. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to all hazmat receipts, storage and movements. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

6. Observe storage limits for the hazmat cage. Store no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Calculate capacity on full-weight pallets: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, so the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets.

7. Stage hazmat only inside the cage. Do not exceed the floor limit. Keep incompatible classes segregated in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response safety data sheets.

8. Execute spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response as follows:
   a) Stop work and alert nearby personnel.
   b) Notify the shift supervisor immediately for incident response.
   c) Ventilate the area and isolate the spill. Do not wash spills into drains.
   d) Don appropriate PPE and deploy the spill kit for the material class.
   e) Contain, absorb and collect the material for safe disposal. Log the incident, quantity and corrective action.

9. Record every PR-12 Cold-chain handling verification and every PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response event in the WMS. Report any limit breach, equipment fault or stock at risk to the shift supervisor for follow-up.

diff.title: 3.2 Hazmat Cage and Spill Response (Zone F)
diff.before:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. The quarantine area is also in Zone F, separate from the cage.

2. Store hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Do not stage hazmat in receiving, bulk storage, picking or dispatch.

3. Do not exceed 3,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage total in the WMS before booking any inbound hazmat for put-away.

4. Obey the pallet limit. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. At this maximum weight the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Report any overweight pallet to the shift supervisor immediately and do not place it in the cage until approved.

5. Wear mandatory PPE on the warehouse floor at all times when handling or working near hazmat. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

6. Follow PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for all hazmat movements, segregation and spill response. Do not open, decant or rework hazmat outside the designated area in Zone F.

7. If a leak, spill or strong odour occurs, stop work and alert persons nearby. Notify the shift supervisor, ventilate and isolate the area, and keep all persons clear of the spill.

8. Do not attempt clean-up without correct PPE and equipment. Don PPE and deploy the spill kit only when authorised, then contain, absorb, collect and log the incident as directed under PR-13.

9. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The warehouse manager retains final sign-off for hazmat storage arrangements and safety controls in Zone F.

10. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Report any damage to the hazmat cage, bunding, signage or ventilation to the maintenance technician and the shift supervisor without delay, and do not use defective equipment.

   a) Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t.

diff.title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
diff.before:
1. The dispatcher is accountable for outbound flow from Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Duties of the dispatcher are:
   1. Book transport for all outbound orders.
   2. Assign dock doors and time slots to carriers.
   3. Release outbound loads under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only when loads are complete and documented.

3. Operate the building's 8 dock doors as a single coordinated plan:
   1. Reserve dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving.
   2. Reserve dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch.
   3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for scheduling.

4. Own the dock schedule:
   1. Assign each carrier a specific door number and time slot.
   2. Balance demand across doors to maintain throughput.
   3. Communicate door assignments to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carriers before loading.

5. Enforce staging discipline in Zone D:
   1. Stage only verified and packed pallets in outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
   2. Do not release loads where picked items have not been scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-04 and PR-05.

6. Apply load limits on every booking:
   1. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
   2. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 26000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions.
   3. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
   4. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg and has 6 pallet positions.
   5. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

7. Plan shift capacity to the proven maximum:
   1. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift.
   2. With 4 outbound dock doors, each taking at most 28 full-weight pallets per trailer, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift.
   3. Do not overbook beyond this limit. Split excess volume to the next shift or add trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit with warehouse manager agreement.

8. Execute PR-06 Outbound dispatch as follows:
   1. Confirm order completeness and packing completion before assigning a door.
   2. Assign door and time slot and record them in the system.
   3. Release the load only after loading and door checks are complete.

9. Coordinate handover at shift change:
   1. Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors.
   2. Hand over open bookings, door allocations, delayed trailers and van commitments.
   3. Ensure no carrier arrives without a confirmed door and time slot.

diff.title: 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits
2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
diff.before:
1. Purpose of the role: unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage, and transfer accepted stock to the correct storage zone without breach of weight, temperature or hazmat limits.

2. Work location and scope: operate solely in Zone A, the receiving zone covering inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving; do not receive inbound goods at any other door. Hand over released pallets only to the designated storage zones: Zone B for bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.

3. Personal compliance on the warehouse floor: wear high-visibility vests at all times as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, and wear safety footwear class S3 as mandatory on the warehouse floor. Remain clear of moving MHE and follow pedestrian controls when working around docks 1-4.

4. Execute PR-01 Inbound receiving in the fixed sequence. Complete the document check BEFORE unloading. Verify purchase order, carrier, quantities and delivery notes against the load while the trailer remains closed. Report discrepancies before breaking the seal or starting unloading.

5. Unload, count and inspect goods in Zone A after the document check passes. Open, count and examine condition, quantity and labelling. Reject damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock from booking and segregate it for quarantine instruction. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01. Do not pre-book unchecked pallets.

6. Use WMS control correctly. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Log counts, inspection results and pallet IDs on the handheld scanner only after physical inspection is complete. Do not create system stock before inspection.

7. Observe pallet limits before release. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check declared weight, re-weigh where required, and do not release overweight pallets for put-away. Report any overweight pallet to the supervisor for correction before PR-02 actions continue.

8. Perform PR-02 Put-away to storage only after system booking. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Print and apply system-directed labels, confirm location tasks on the scanner, and move pallets to the WMS-directed bay in Zone B or other assigned zone. Do not stage inbound stock in aisles or dispatch areas as put-away.

9. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for chilled inbound. Transfer accepted chilled goods immediately to Zone E, the cold zone held at +2 to +6 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C. Keep cold-chain pallets closed, minimise door openings, and record handover to Zone E so temperature control is maintained.

10. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for hazmat receipts. Route directed hazmat to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The hazmat cage covers 60 m2 inside Zone F and no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage stock on the WMS before put-away and do not exceed the limit. If leaking, odorous or damaged hazmat is found, stop work, contain the area and alert the shift supervisor; do not inspect or open damaged hazmat on the general bench.

11. Maintain inbound discipline: keep Zone A clear for inspection and unloading, return equipment and scanners to charge, and ensure all inspected goods are either booked and tasked for put-away or formally segregated before leaving the zone at shift end.

diff.title: 1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs
diff.before:
1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs

Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates receiving from its 6,000 m2 warehouse floor. The building provides 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller, and inbound receiving is confined to a defined allocation and sequence.

1. Door allocation for inbound. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving exclusively. No inbound unloading will be scheduled to other doors.
2. Receiving hours. Standard receiving windows align with staffed shifts:
   a) Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday.
   b) Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
   Arrivals outside these windows or requiring extended handling will be accepted only where overtime has been agreed in advance. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3. Scheduling ownership. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and for inbound this includes confirming the allocated door in Zone A and the booked arrival slot before arrival.
4. Resource commitment. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Harborwick commits trained inbound operators to each booked receiving slot during the windows above.
5. Receiving sequence under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Harborwick will apply the following mandatory order for every inbound load:
   a) Document check happens before unloading.
   b) Inbound goods are inspected before they are booked into the system.
   No goods will be unloaded prior to document verification, and no system receipt will be posted prior to physical inspection and count.
6. Booking to put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage. Put-away from Zone A to bulk or other storage will commence only after the WMS receipt is created under PR-01.
7. Load limits applicable at receiving. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Harborwick will weigh-check and reject or rework overweight pallets at Zone A before system booking, and will notify the client of any non-conformance identified during inspection.

Commitment: Harborwick will make Zone A and dock doors 1-4 available as scheduled, staff receiving with inbound operators during Shift 1 and Shift 2, and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage in the exact order stated above for every inbound delivery.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 4 loads per shift multiplied by 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 12 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

diff.title: 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
diff.before:
2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level

1. Picking operations are performed in Zone C, which is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and no picking is performed from bulk storage locations.

2. Harbourwick commits to full scan-verified picking for every order under PR-04 Order picking. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and no tote or order will be released to packing without successful WMS verification. Packing and labelling under PR-05 Packing and labelling is then completed as a committed service step prior to dispatch.

3. Pick face availability is assured through PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, and picking will not commence on incomplete faces. This sequencing ensures order accuracy and prevents short picks due to empty locations.

4. The facility supporting this service level comprises a warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 with high-bay pallet racking in Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, providing 2,400 pallet positions for reserve stock. Replenishment moves stock from Zone B to Zone C to maintain pick face accuracy.

5. To sustain accurate and safe picking, Harbourwick maintains compliant infrastructure and handling limits at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, with segregated pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m wide maintained and kept clear. MHE and pedestrian segregation is enforced to protect picking accuracy and prevent location errors.

6. Pallet and racking limits are enforced as part of inventory integrity. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, and any pallet exceeding this limit will be held for rework and not made available for picking.

7. Picking is executed with 20 handheld WMS scanners shared by pickers and inbound staff, ensuring every pick movement is system-directed and verified. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, and will investigate any scan discrepancy, location error or quantity variance identified during PR-03 or PR-04 execution.

8. Harbourwick commits to maintaining stock controller oversight of all replenishment and picking accuracy exceptions, with accurate WMS stock reflecting verified picks, replenishments and packing activity in Zone C.

diff.title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. shall handle all damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and shall move such stock to quarantine on the same day it is identified.

2. All goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 shall be held in the quarantine area in Zone F until inspection, approval and posting are complete. Zone F holds the value-added services area and is the sole quarantine location for damaged goods pending disposition.

3. The quarantine process shall be controlled as follows:
  a) The shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response shall be notified immediately of any damage and shall direct placement into the quarantine area in Zone F and review the related reports.
  b) The warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs shall retain final authority for write-offs above threshold and for overall compliance of quarantine handling.
  c) No quarantined stock shall be moved to bulk storage, picking or dispatch staging without recorded approval under PR-09.

4. Write-off approvals for damaged goods shall follow defined financial thresholds:
  a) The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR.
  b) Damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves such cases. For damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR the shift supervisor must endorse the request and forward it to the warehouse manager for final decision.
  c) Harborwick shall not process any write-off above 750 EUR without that approval recorded in the system.

5. Where damaged goods include hazmat, Harborwick shall stage and store such stock only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and shall contain no more than 3,000 kg of hazmat at one time. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, therefore the hazmat cage holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Harborwick commits to enforce this limit and to reject or re-allocate any quantity that would exceed it, reporting the condition immediately.

6. Harborwick shall maintain traceability of all quarantined stock in Zone F, including photographic evidence where required, WMS posting of inspection outcomes, and retention of labels for audit. Disposition to restock, rework or scrap shall only occur after the applicable approver under paragraph 4 has authorised it.

diff.title: Docks and Yard Access
diff.before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

7. For outbound operations, stage loads in Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 512 full-weight pallets per shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 512 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 12 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

diff.title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
diff.before:
1. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep its three functions physically separate and clearly signed: the quarantine area, the returns inspection area and the hazmat cage.

2. The quarantine area is in Zone F. Use it only for goods held under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and for any stock awaiting a quality or stock-controller decision. Do not put away quarantined pallets to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E. Do not release quarantined stock until the hold is lifted in the system.

3. Inspect all returns in Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each item. Place the inspected goods in the quarantine area when they cannot be returned directly to stock. Obtain the required approval before any restock, rework or scrap decision.

4. Handle damaged goods under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Move damaged pallets to the quarantine area in Zone F immediately. Record the damage, quantity and location in the WMS. Do not dispose, rework or restock until the authorised approver has signed the disposition.

5. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 and is locked at all times except during authorised put-away or picking. Permit entry only to trained operators listed on the hazmat authorisation roster. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every movement, storage check and spill.

6. Observe the stock limit for the hazmat cage at all times:
   a) No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
   b) A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg.
   c) The hazmat cage therefore holds at most 3 full-weight pallets. Calculate the remaining capacity before each put-away and do not exceed the 3,000 kg limit, even if floor space remains.

7. Complete system booking before any put-away to the cage. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Then execute PR-02 Put-away to storage:
   a) Verify the booking, hazard class and weight on the handheld.
   b) Transport the pallet to Zone F on the designated hazmat route.
   c) Place the pallet only in the assigned cage location and confirm the put-away by scan.

8. Maintain segregation and housekeeping in Zone F:
   a) Never store hazmat outside the cage, even temporarily.
   b) Never store non-hazmat goods inside the cage.
   c) Keep spill kits, fire extinguishers and safety data sheets at the cage entrance as defined in PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
   d) Keep the quarantine area clear of outbound staging. Outbound staging uses the area in front of docks 5-8. There are 4 outbound dock doors and outbound loads are not to be staged in Zone F.

9. Report any over-limit, damaged packaging or suspected leak in Zone F to the shift supervisor immediately and initiate PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Do not attempt to move leaking containers without the correct PPE and containment.

diff.title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity

1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 32 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Do not exceed either the payload limit or the floor positions. For full-weight pallets, plan to a maximum of 32 pallets per trailer.

   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.

Check both weight and floor positions before assigning the van. If the order exceeds 2 full-weight pallets, book trailer capacity and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.

With 5 doors each handling 4 loads of 32 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 640 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 640 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

Do not exceed the calculated ceiling without prior agreement. Record all bookings in the WMS and refer excess demand to the next available shift.

10. Respect hazmat constraints when staging mixed loads. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage inside Zone F at one time. At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 3 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). Do not allocate hazmat pallets to a trailer until cage stock is confirmed within limit.

Stage hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Confirm the cage total is within limit before building any outbound hazmat load.

11. Record trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts in the WMS before releasing the vehicle. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

diff.title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 800 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 32 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 512 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 4 loads per shift multiplied by 32 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 12 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 512 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

diff.title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
diff.before:
1. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.

Zone B holds the site's primary pallet inventory. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for standard pallets. All put-away to this zone follows PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away.

Do not move goods to Zone B until the WMS booking is confirmed. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Use the designated main transport aisles to transfer booked pallets from receiving into Zone B.

3. Observe bay load and pallet weight limits in every location.

Check the bay label before placing stock. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Calculate the total bay load before adding a pallet and leave the bay empty if the limit would be exceeded.

4. Use the correct truck for the task and aisle.

Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Operate counterbalance forklifts in the main aisles and approach bays squarely. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for transport and low-level placement. The fleet has 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays. Select the reach truck for any placement above lower levels and verify capacity against pallet weight before lifting.

5. Apply block-stacking limits where free stacking is authorised.

Where pallets are approved for free block-stacking outside racking, observe both limits together. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Stop stacking when either limit is reached and report any leaning or damaged stack to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Maintain access and inspection readiness.

Keep main aisles and rack storage aisles clear of staging, waste or trailing equipment. Position pallets fully within beams with no overhang into the aisle envelope. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Do not use any bay marked as damaged or under inspection and log defects for the maintenance technician without delay.

diff.title: Electric Fleet
diff.before:
1. Fleet inventory for internal transport is fixed and fully electric for powered trucks. Do not exceed rated capacities or site weight limits when planning lifts and storage.

2. Counterbalance forklifts: the fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts. Each unit is rated at 3.0 t. Use these trucks for dock work, yard movements and bulk transport between zones.

3. Reach trucks: the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays. Each reach truck is rated at 2.0 t. Reserve reach trucks for racking operations in the high-bay areas where height and aisle width require them.

4. Electric pallet jacks: the fleet has 11 electric pallet jacks. Assign these units to horizontal movements of full pallets, replenishment support and outbound staging.

5. Hand pallet jacks: the site has 12 hand pallet jacks. Keep these units distributed across receiving, picking and dispatch for short moves and manual handling where powered equipment is not required.

6. Personnel authorised to operate this equipment are defined by role. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. No other role may operate MHE unless authorised separately.

7. Pallet weight limit applies to every load moved by any truck. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Check the declared weight in the WMS before lifting and reject any pallet stated above this limit for standard handling.

8. Racking load limit applies to every bay in bulk storage. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate total bay load from pallet weights and pallet positions before put-away and do not exceed the bay rating.

9. Hazmat storage limit applies to the cage in Zone F. No more than 3,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Monitor cumulative hazmat weight on receipt and during put-away to remain within the cage limit.

10. Handheld WMS scanners support all moves. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Book equipment out at shift start and return units to charge at shift end; report faults to the shift supervisor immediately.

11. Match truck to task by weight and location. Use counterbalance trucks for general transport, reach trucks for high-bay placement, and pallet jacks for low-level moves. Never substitute a lower-rated truck to lift a load beyond its rating.

12. Maintain availability through correct charging and parking. Park powered trucks in designated charging lanes at breaks and at end of shift. Keep hand pallet jacks clear of aisles and pedestrian walkways when not in use.

diff.title: Racking and Equipment Maintenance
diff.before:
1. Maintain racking, MHE and dock equipment to a safe, serviceable standard. Keep all storage within rated limits and keep a complete record of inspections and repairs.
2. Assign the maintenance technician to maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and to log all repairs. Do not operate damaged racking, levellers or trucks until the maintenance technician has inspected and cleared them.
3. Carry out a documented safety inspection of all racking every month. Include uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, anchors and beam locks in Zone B and any other racked locations.
4. Record the monthly inspection by bay, level and date. Photograph defects, grade the damage and tag the bay out of use where required. Enter the result in the repair log on the same day.
5. Log every repair against the original defect. State the fault found, parts fitted, date completed and name of the maintenance technician. Close the tag only when the repair is verified and the log is signed.
6. Enforce bay load limits at all times. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Do not exceed the posted bay label. Redistribute or offload overweight bays immediately and report the occurrence for correction.
7. Apply block-stack limits where pallets are free block-stacked outside racking. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. Measure from floor to top of load. Restack any non-compliant stack before leaving the area.
8. Include MHE and dock equipment in the inspection cycle. The fleet has 9 electric counterbalance forklifts and the fleet has 5 reach trucks for the high bays; check steering, brakes, forks, chains, hydraulics and safety devices. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; check leveller plates, lips, pits, controls and edge guards.
9. Coordinate MHE checks with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Report defects found during daily checks under PR-10 to the maintenance technician without delay. Take unserviceable trucks out of service, isolate the keys and update the log.
10. Review the repair log at each monthly inspection. Verify that outstanding actions are closed, recurring damage is investigated and preventive measures are applied to protect racking and equipment.

diff.title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply these limits to all racking in Zone B and to any free block stack on the floor. No pallet, including its load, may weigh more than 800 kg.

2. Do not exceed the rack bay limit. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Check the bay load plate before placing pallets and count the gross weight of every pallet in the bay against this limit.

3. Because the maximum pallet weight is 800 kg, a bay loaded with full-weight pallets can hold no more than three pallets. Three pallets at 800 kg equals 2,400 kg and stays within the 2,700 kg bay limit. Reduce the number of pallets or the weight per pallet to stay within the limit.

4. Observe equipment limits when handling stock for racking:
   a) Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t.
   b) Reach trucks for the high bays are rated at 2.0 t.
   Do not use equipment beyond its rated capacity to place or retrieve pallets.

5. Respect free block-stacking limits where pallets are not racked:
   a) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3.5 m in height.
   b) Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
   Both limits apply at the same time. Stop stacking when either limit is reached. Stack only on a level, stable floor and interlock tiers where the product allows.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Use only designated pallet positions in Zone B and do not stage unracked pallets in rack aisles.

7. Keep aisles clear for safe transport and access:
   a) Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
   b) Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
   Do not encroach on aisle markings with overhanging pallets, wrappers or staging. Maintain clear sightlines at aisle intersections.

8. Report any rack damage immediately. Do not load, unload or pass under a damaged bay. Segregate the bay and apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for any affected stock. Move damaged or suspect pallets to the quarantine process and do not return them to racking until inspected.

9. Maintain racking integrity through scheduled checks. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. Cooperate with the inspection and remove loads as directed to allow access.
